filters, masked). An unmasked task writes its own audit record as well (action
export_unmasked: task id, resource, reason and, once generated, the row count; never a
value).
Quarterly tax export (`resource=tax_withdrawals`, BR-WDR-21): `filters.quarter` selects the
natural quarter by `paid_at` (+08:00).
Masked version: `export` and `fund.view`, no step-up, no `reason` (`reason` without
`unmasked: true` is 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`).
Full version `unmasked: true`: `tax.export_full` alone (a super admin holds it; `export` is
not needed as well, and no `fund.*` point implies it), a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token`
(missing, expired or lower → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`) and `reason` (1–200 characters,
the purpose BR-WDR-21 asks for; missing → 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`).
File: line one is a note (the creator's account name and the export time), the header
follows on line two (for this resource only). Columns: name, identity number, income type,
income, tax withheld, paid time, payee account (masked), out_biz_no, realname correction
after payment (empty if none, else the correction time). Amounts are integer fen. The
masked version shows the identity number as first 6 and last 4 and the name in full. The
identity is the user's current one (agent default, awaiting finance's confirmation).
A realname that cannot be read fails the whole task; so does exceeding
`admin.export.max_rows`, without truncating, and its failure_reason says to raise that
configuration key.
Audit: export_create; the full version also export_unmasked (with the row count and the
purpose); a masked `tax_withdrawals` task writes its own audit record when generated
(action export_generated: task id, resource, row count, the creator as actor, no purpose).
Other resources follow the rules above.
Limits are configuration keys whose default values the implementation sets:
`admin.export.max_rows` (rows per file; a task with more rows fails with a failure_reason
saying so, narrow the filters) and `admin.export.max_running_per_admin` (tasks of one
creator generated at the same time; the rest stay pending until a slot frees up).
Lifecycle (enum export_status): pending → running → done or failed; done → expired 24
hours after the file was generated (BR-ID-30 ⑨, the object-storage lifecycle rule deletes
the file); pending or running → cancelled when the creator's account is disabled (with an
audit record); failed → pending by POST /admin/v1/exports/{id}/retry. There is no cancel
operation.

get.summary: List export tasks (own tasks, or everyone's with audit.view_all)
get.description:
An account with `tax.export_full` and without
`export` passes this point too and sees only its own `tax_withdrawals` tasks.
Permission point `export` (04 §11.1; no step-up); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Tasks of the console's app, newest first
(`created_at` descending, then the server's internal order for the same time), page by page
(`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200, above that 20001).
Visibility (enforced by the server, BR-ID-34 细则「后台导出任务」): an account holding
`audit.view_all` (a super admin holds every point) sees every account's tasks, their
filters summary and status; an account without it only sees the tasks it created.
`audit.view_all` only widens this list: downloading and retrying stay limited to the
creator (GET /admin/v1/exports/{id}/download, POST /admin/v1/exports/{id}/retry).
Filters combine with AND: `status` (enum export_status), `resource` (enum
export_resource), `from` (inclusive) and `to` (exclusive) on `created_at`, ISO 8601 times
with offset (04 §5); `from` later than `to` is 20001 with `data.fields=[from, to]`.
Rows never carry the download link; status names come from BR-TEXT-25
admin_dict.export_status. Listing does not write an audit record.

parameters.description: Only tasks in this status (enum export_status).

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Only tasks of this source list (enum export_resource).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Earliest creation time, inclusive (ISO 8601 with offset).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Latest creation time, exclusive (ISO 8601 with offset).

get.summary: Get a short-lived signed link to the file of one's own finished export (audited)
get.description:
For `tax_withdrawals` tasks (BR-WDR-21) `tax.export_full` also passes this point; any
task it cannot act on (an unknown id, another account's task, another resource) is 20001
with `data.fields=[id]`, like the rest. The source-list permission of that resource is
`fund.view`, or `tax.export_full` for a full file (`masked=false`).
Permission point `export` (04 §11.1; no step-up); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Only the creator of the task can download it, even
with `audit.view_all` (BR-ID-34 细则「后台导出任务」). Every call is authorized again and
signs a new link; no long-lived link is issued. The server also checks that the creator
still holds the permission of the source list (`users` → `user.list`) and, for an unmasked
file (`masked=false`), still holds the pii point it was made under (`pii.reveal_phone`, or
`tax.export_full` for a `tax_withdrawals` file).
Another account's task, an unknown id, a task of another app, and a creator who no longer
holds those points are all 20001 with `data.fields=[id]` (no probing).
Only a task in status done whose `expires_at` has not passed can be downloaded; any other
status is 30417 with `data.status` (pending, running, failed, expired, cancelled; a done
task past `expires_at` answers expired even before the server has set the status).
The link `url` is valid until `url_expires_at` = min(5 minutes from now, the task's
`expires_at`), so a disabled or demoted creator loses access within minutes.
Every call that returns a link writes its own audit record (action export_download: task
id, resource, masked; never the link) before the response is sent. The response carries
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: A freshly signed link to the CSV file.

Cache-Control.description: Always no-store; the signed link is not cached by any proxy or the browser.

post.summary: Retry one's own failed export task
post.description:
For `tax_withdrawals` tasks (BR-WDR-21) `tax.export_full` also passes this point; any
task it cannot act on (an unknown id, another account's task, another resource) is 20001
with `data.fields=[id]`, like the rest. The source-list permission of that resource is
`fund.view`, or `tax.export_full` for a full file (`masked=false`).
Permission point `export` (04 §11.1); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Only the creator of the task can retry it, even with
`audit.view_all`: another account's task, an unknown id or a task of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[id]` (no probing; BR-ID-34 细则「后台导出任务」).
Only a failed task can be retried; any other status is 30417 with `data.status` (pending,
running, done, expired, cancelled; the same code as a download in the wrong status).
The checks of creating are made again on the caller's current points: the permission of
the source list (`users` → `user.list`) and, for an unmasked task (`masked=false`),
`pii.reveal_phone` (`tax.export_full` for a `tax_withdrawals` task), both 10403 when lacking. An unmasked task also needs a new totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` (missing, expired or lower → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`) and a new
`reason` (1–200 characters; missing → 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`): every
generation of a file with full values is verified anew. A masked task takes an empty body;
`reason` there is 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]` and no step-up token is checked.
The task keeps its id, resource, filters and masked flag and goes back to pending
(`progress`, `failure_reason` cleared); the response is the task as it is now. Retrying
writes an audit record (action export_retry: task id, resource, masked), and an unmasked
task its own record with the new reason (action export_unmasked). No Idempotency-Key
(04 §6.6): a second call while the task is pending again is 30417.

Permission point `fund.view` (04 §6.6 invite-rewards, 01 F-ADM-27; read only, no step-up);

get.summary: Top-bar search by a full order number, withdrawal number, phone number or UID
get.description:
The console's top-bar search (01 F-ADM-04; 04 §6.6 search; BR-ID-34 细则「一框搜」). Any
signed-in admin may call it (read only, no step-up); what comes back is trimmed by the
server to three permission points, one per hit type (enum admin_search_hit_type): order
`order.view`, user `user.lookup`, withdrawal `fund.view`. A super admin holds every point.

`q` is trimmed of surrounding whitespace and must then be 1–64 characters, else 20001 with
`data.fields=[q]`. The server tells from its shape what `q` is and matches the full value
only (no prefix or partial match): an order number (the order's full number), a withdrawal
number (its full number; no hit until the withdrawal module ships), a full phone number
(normalised as in BR-ID-05 细则「手机号规范化」) or a UID (the user_id, a UUID). Only
objects of the console's app are found. Input of no recognised shape is not an error: 200
with an empty list.

Anti-probing (BR-ID-34 细则「一框搜」): no hit and no permission look the same. A hit of a
type the account has no point for is dropped silently; when nothing is left the response is
200 with `items=[]` and `truncated=false`. The operation never answers 10403
`admin_permission_denied` (10403 only for `admin_ip_not_allowed`, common to every admin
operation) and never 20001 for an unknown number, unlike GET /admin/v1/users/lookup.

`items[]` lists the hits (`type`, `id` for the detail route, `summary` a masked one-line
summary: phone numbers masked 3 + 4 as BR-ID-33, no full phone, identity or payout account
number). An order or withdrawal hit is followed by its owner as a `user` item, trimmed by
`user.lookup` like any user hit. At most 10 items; when there are more, the first 10 come
back with `truncated=true` (the console asks for a more complete number). The console
opens the detail page directly when exactly one item comes back and lists candidates
otherwise.

Audit: a search by full phone number that returns a user writes an audit entry, as a
lookup by phone through `user.lookup` does (04 §6.6 search). Other searches are not
audited.

200.description: The hits the account may see; empty for no hit and for no permission alike.

empty.summary: No hit, or hits only of types the account has no permission point for

(`[uid]` or `[phone]`). Returns the user as GET /admin/v1/users/{user_id} does, with the
phone number masked (the full number only through POST /admin/v1/users/{user_id}/reveal).
Lookup by order number comes with the order console.

get.description:
Permission point `user.list` or `user.lookup` (either is enough; 04 §11.1; read only, no
step-up). An unknown `user_id`, or one of another app, is 20001 with
`data.fields=[user_id]`. Non-sensitive fields only: the phone number is masked 3 + 4
(BR-ID-33) and the full number is only shown through POST

nulls and `row_version` null when the user has none yet; a row, even a first one at

ledger and withdrawals of the user come with the order and fund consoles and are not part
of this schema yet.
CT-26k (D10-517) adds the 「基本信息」 fields of the console's user detail:
`realname_status`, `masked_name` and `masked_id_no` (BR-ID-33: name with only the last
character, ID number first 1 + last 1; both null unless realname_status is verified) and
`payout_account` (the current payout account masked as in GET /v1/me/payout-account, null
when none is bound), plus `deletion_status` (the user's latest deletion request, BR-ID-27 /
BR-ID-28; null when none). The full values stay with the audited reveal. This operation
is implemented; the five new fields are 实现另单 and stay optional until that
implementation is merged.

put.summary: Ban, unban, freeze or unfreeze a user
put.description:
Permission point by `action` (04 §11.2): `ban` and `unban` need `risk.ban`, `freeze` and
`unfreeze` need `risk.freeze`; lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier for every action (without a
valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). An unknown `user_id`
is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`.
Body checks (20001 with `data.fields` naming the field): `reason` is required (1–200
characters); `reason_category` (enum risk_reason_category, BR-TEXT-23 细则「原因类别」) is
required for `ban` and `freeze` and not accepted for `unban` and `unfreeze`;
`frozen_until` is only accepted for `freeze`, null or absent means a freeze without end
(BR-ID-36), and a value must be later than the server's current time (no upper bound).
State rules (44004 without data otherwise): `ban` from normal or frozen; `freeze` from
normal or frozen (on a frozen user it rewrites `frozen_until`, `reason_category` and
`reason`); `unban` only from banned; `unfreeze` only from frozen. A banned user is not
frozen directly (unban first); an appealing user is refused for every action, the appeal
is concluded through the appeal console instead (BR-ID-36).
CAS: `expected_row_version` is `risk.row_version` of GET /admin/v1/users/{user_id}. null
means "the console saw no risk-state row" and only creates the user's first row while
there is still none; an integer only matches the row's current `row_version`. Every other
case is 20902 with `data.resource=user_risk_state`, refresh and retry (04 §6.6): null
while a row exists (row_version 0 included, someone created it meanwhile), an integer
while there is no row, or an integer other than the current one. State rules are judged
on the state as read (no row = normal).
Effects (BR-ID-31, BR-ID-36), in one transaction with the state change: `ban` revokes
every session and refresh token of the user and sets the user's active and invalid union
bindings to blocked with blocked_reason ban (a binding already blocked keeps its reason);
new withdrawal requests are refused with 10006, existing withdrawals are not changed; a
ban has no end. `unban` sets the bindings blocked for ban back: a taobao binding becomes
invalid (the user authorizes again), a binding on any other platform (such as pdd, which
has no re-authorization) becomes active and takes effect at once (BR-ID-20). `freeze` and
`unfreeze` touch neither sessions nor bindings
(withdrawals 30303 and held credits follow from the state, BR-WDR-05, BR-CALC-13); a
freeze with `frozen_until` ends by itself at that time. Every action writes an audit
record (action user_risk_state_change, before and after state, reason category and
reason). After the risk state changes, the notification module sends the in-app message
RISK_STATE_CHANGED (BR-TEXT-23; a ban notice becomes visible only after the unban,
BR-ID-31); this operation does not send it and its response does not wait for the
sending. The response is the risk state as it is now. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

post.summary: Reset a user's union authorization (release the binding)
post.description:
Permission point `union.binding_reset` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). Reset is the console's "unbind the
taobao filing" (解绑淘宝备案) in the user's filing details, for correcting a wrong binding
(OPS-11); users cannot unbind or rebind themselves (BR-ID-19, BR-ID-20). `reason` is
required (1–200 characters, else 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`). An unknown `user_id`
is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`. Reset exists for `platform=taobao` only: any other
platform is 20001 with `data.fields=[platform]`, the same as a platform without user
authorization (such as jd); pdd and other unions have no re-authorization, so their
bindings are only disabled and enabled (BR-ID-20).
State rule (BR-ID-20): only an active or invalid binding is reset; a blocked one (any
blocked_reason), a released one, or no binding row on that platform is 30154 without data.
The binding becomes released with released_at = now and cooldown_until = released_at +
`bind.rebind_cooldown_days` (BR-ID-19; orders keep attributing by BR-ATTR-07); the user's
cached converted links are cleared (BR-AI-04 细则「转链缓存」), and the next purchase asks for
authorization again (30101).
CAS: `expected_row_version` is the binding's `row_version` from GET
/admin/v1/users/{user_id}; a mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=union_binding`, refresh
and retry (04 §6.6).
A binding row created later on the same platform (after a release) never reuses a
row_version the platform's earlier rows had: it starts after the highest one, so a stale
value never matches the newer row.
Writes an audit record (action union_binding_reset, before and after
status, reason). The response is the binding as it is now. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

post.summary: Stop rebates for a user's union binding (停用返利)
post.description:
Permission point `union.binding_disable` (04 §11.2, shared with enable); lacking it is
10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (without a valid
totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). `reason` is required (1–200
characters, else 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`). An unknown `user_id` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[user_id]`; a platform without user authorization (such as jd) is 20001 with
`data.fields=[platform]`.
State rule (BR-ID-20, OPS-11): only an active or invalid binding is disabled; a blocked
one (any blocked_reason, admin_disable included), a released one, or no binding row on
that platform is 30154 without data. The binding becomes blocked with blocked_reason
admin_disable; it is never released by itself and only POST
…/union-bindings/{platform}/enable brings it back (on taobao as invalid, on other
platforms as active, see enable). While it is blocked the user's purchase entry answers
30153 (BR-ID-17, BR-ID-18).
CAS: `expected_row_version` is the binding's `row_version`; a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=union_binding` (04 §6.6). As for reset, a later binding row on the platform
never reuses an earlier row's row_version. Writes an audit record (action
union_binding_disable, before and after status, reason). The response is the binding as
it is now. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

post.summary: Restore rebates for a disabled union binding (恢复返利)
post.description:
Permission point `union.binding_disable` (04 §11.2, shared with disable); lacking it is
10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (without a valid
totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). `reason` is required (1–200
characters, else 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`). An unknown `user_id` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[user_id]`; a platform without user authorization (such as jd) is 20001 with
`data.fields=[platform]`.
State rule (BR-ID-20): only a binding blocked with blocked_reason admin_disable is
enabled; any other status, a binding blocked for ban or deletion, or no binding row on
that platform is 30154 without data (a binding blocked for ban comes back through unban
only). On taobao the binding becomes invalid: the user authorizes again (30102 at the next
purchase) before rebates resume. On any other platform (such as pdd, which has no
re-authorization: the user authorizes once) it becomes active and rebates resume at once,
without asking the user to authorize again (BR-ID-20).
A user whose risk state is banned is refused with 30154 without data whatever the
binding's blocked_reason: while the ban lasts every binding of the user stays blocked
(BR-ID-31), and a ban followed by deletion releases nothing by itself (BR-ID-20). The
binding operations of the admin console and ban / unban are serialized per user, so
concurrent requests on the same user never leave a banned user with an invalid binding.
CAS: `expected_row_version` is the binding's `row_version`; a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=union_binding` (04 §6.6). As for reset, a later binding row on the platform
never reuses an earlier row's row_version. Writes an audit record (action
union_binding_enable, before and after status, reason). The response is the binding as it
is now. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

example.reason: 核实为本人账号，恢复返利

200.description: The binding as it is now (taobao: invalid until the user authorizes again; other: active).

data.reason: 核实为本人账号，恢复返利

get.summary: A user's direct invitees, page by page (masked)
get.description:
Permission point `user.lookup` or `user.list` (either is enough; 04 §6.6
users/{id}/invitees; read only, no step-up); lacking both is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. An unknown `user_id`, or one of another app, is
20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`. Lists the user's direct invitees: the users of the
console's app whose current inviter (users.parent_id, the current value only, BR-INV-11)
is this user. A former invitee moved to another inviter through POST
/admin/v1/users/{user_id}/inviter is no longer listed, and indirect invitees are not
listed. Latest bound first (users.parent_bound_at descending, then user_id), page by page
(`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200). Rows hold the fields of 04 §6.6 only: `user_id`,
`phone_masked` (3 + 4, BR-ID-33; the full number only through POST
/admin/v1/users/{user_id}/reveal), `nickname`, `registered_at` and `level`. No member-tier
fields (BR-INV-23 is not shown in this phase). The bind source and bind time of each row
are not part of 04 §6.6 and are pending.

post.summary: Change a user's distribution level (调等级)
post.description:
Permission point `user.level` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). In the MVP a level only changes through
this operation, with step-up and a reason (BR-INV-14); automatic promotion is P1.
Body checks (20001 with `data.fields` naming the field): `level` is required and only
L1, L2 or L3 (enum user_level, BR-INV-14); `reason` is required (1–200 characters). An
unknown `user_id` is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`. A level whose status in the
levels table is disabled is 20001 with `data.fields=[level]`: no user enters a disabled
level, users already on it keep it (BR-INV-14). The user's current level is 20001 with
`data.fields=[level]` as well (nothing is changed or logged).
Effects (BR-INV-14), in one transaction: users.level becomes `level` and one
level_change_logs row is written (user_id, before, after, source, operator, reason,
effective_at); a console change has effective_at = created_at = the time of submission
(+08:00). The new level only applies to orders with paid_at ≥ effective_at (BR-CALC-12,
the equal instant takes the new level); existing commission snapshots are not
recalculated, and quotes use the current level at once. The level is not shown in the
app (OPS-20). Writes an audit record (action user_level_change, before and after level,
reason). The response is the user as GET /admin/v1/users/{user_id} returns it now.
A compare-and-set value with its 20902 conflict is pending: 04 §3.2 users has no
row_version and contracts/error-codes.yaml 20902 has no resource for a user's level.
No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

post.summary: Change or remove a user's inviter (改上级)
post.description:
Permission point `user.inviter` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). Users never change or remove their own
inviter (BR-INV-10); this is the console's change of inviter, removal included
(`inviter_user_id: null` leaves the user without an inviter). `reason` is required (1–200
characters, else 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`). An unknown `user_id` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[user_id]`.
Order of checks, the first hit is returned (BR-INV-10): permission, step-up and reason
(10403, 10003, 20001) → the target user has no direct invitee, no order (any status; an
UNATTRIBUTED order has no user and does not count, BR-INV-07 细则) and no claim in any
status, else 30409 → the new inviter (`inviter_user_id`) is a user of the console's app
and inviter_unavailable is false (BR-INV-02), else 30401; an unknown inviter_user_id is
30401 too, never 20001; skipped when removing → relation conflict (BR-INV-08: the new
inviter is the target user, an invitee of the target at any depth, or shares a device
with the target; the operator's device is not added to the target's device set), else
30403; skipped when removing. 30401 does not tell the reason. The change is not bound by
the backfill window (BR-INV-07, 30404) nor by growth.invite_bind.enabled (30408 never
comes back here). Setting the user's current inviter again, or removing on a user
without an inviter, is not defined by BR-INV-10 and is pending.
Effects (BR-INV-10), in one transaction: users.parent_id becomes `inviter_user_id`,
self_bind_used = true, parent_bind_source = admin, parent_bound_at = the time of the
operation, and one relation_change_logs row is written (user_id, old and new parent,
source admin, operator, reason, created_at +08:00). After a removal the user gets no
self-binding chance again (POST /v1/me/inviter answers 30402). Commission snapshots
already written do not change; an order paid before the change keeps the inviter of its
paid_at (BR-INV-13, BR-CALC-12). Writes an audit record (action user_inviter_change, old
and new inviter, reason). The response is the user as GET /admin/v1/users/{user_id}
returns it now. A compare-and-set value with its 20902 conflict is pending: 04 §3.2 users
has no row_version and contracts/error-codes.yaml 20902 has no resource for a user's
inviter. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

patch.summary: Edit a user's phone number and nickname (编辑会员信息)
patch.description:
Permission point `user.phone_change` (04 §11.2; since 2026-10-05 it covers the nickname as
well, the key is unchanged); lacking it is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`.
Step-up: totp tier (without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`). The console's edit of member information after the customer service
checked the user's identity in the WeCom conversation (BR-ID-06 细则「客服代办换号」,
BR-ID-39 细则「后台改昵称」): only `phone` and `nickname` are edited here, the real-name
data goes through `user.realname_fix` (BR-ID-25) and the balance through `fund.adjust`
(BR-FUND-24). The save takes effect at once and the new number is not verified: no SMS to
it, no confirmation in the app, no code asked of the user.
Body checks (20001 with `data.fields` naming the field): `reason` is required (1–200
characters; what was checked in the WeCom conversation); at least one of `phone` and
`nickname`, neither is 20001 with `data.fields=[phone, nickname]`; `phone` is normalised as
in BR-ID-05 细则「手机号规范化」, a result that is not a mainland mobile number is 20001
with `data.fields=[phone]` and `data.reason=phone_invalid`; `nickname`, trimmed of leading
and trailing white space, must be 1–16 extended grapheme clusters, else 20001 with
`data.fields=[nickname]` (BR-ID-39). An unknown `user_id`, or one of another app, is 20001
with `data.fields=[user_id]`.
Unchanged fields: a field equal to the user's current value is treated as not edited — the
phone compared after normalisation with the current number, the nickname after trimming.
A field not edited is not written, triggers no session revocation, no blacklist or
occupancy check and no content-safety review.
Checks of an edited phone, in this order (BR-ID-06): the number is blacklisted → 44001;
the number belongs to another account of this app, judged by the normalised phone_hmac
and including accounts in the deletion cooling period or processing → 30411 without
`data.reason` (never `mergeable`: the console does not merge accounts, a merge only
happens with the user's own confirmation). The number of an account whose deletion is
complete may be used. An edited nickname then goes through content-safety text review: a
hit, or a review that times out (fail-close), is 20001 with
`data.reason=nickname_sensitive`. Any of these refuses the whole save; nothing is
written.
Effects, in one transaction: an edited phone overwrites users.phone_cipher / phone_hmac,
the old phone_hmac is written to deleted_identities (reason=phone_changed, retention
BR-ID-30), and every session of the user is revoked (each device's refresh-token family
and session sid, as in BR-ID-07); the user signs in again with the new number, the
revoked devices get 10404. Access tokens already issued expire by their BR-ID-07
lifetime. A nickname-only edit revokes nothing. An edited nickname is not counted in the
user's 3 changes per natural month (BR-ID-39) and does not use up the user's remaining
changes (no 30415 here). Every successful save writes one audit record (action
user_profile_edit: admin, reason, the fields actually changed with before and after
values, phone numbers masked 3 + 4; with no field changed the changed fields are empty).
Retrying a save that already took effect therefore returns the same user and only adds
an audit record. The response is the user as GET /admin/v1/users/{user_id} returns it
now, phone number masked, plus `changed_fields` (CT-26k, D10-517): the fields this save
actually changed (`phone`, `nickname`; the same list as the audit record), an empty
array when nothing changed, so a retry tells the console that nothing was changed this
time. This operation is implemented; `changed_fields` is 实现另单 and stays optional
until that implementation is merged. No compare-and-set value and no Idempotency-Key
(04 §6.6).
Pending re-verification (BR-WDR-01 细则「旧手机号被二次放号时的提现加验」, 清除标记只走人工;
BR-ID-44; contract CT-26j, implemented by a later task): when the edited phone is saved
for an account that carries the "pending re-verification" flag, the same transaction
(together with the session revocation above) also unbinds every third-party identity
(user_oauth row) of the user that is not among the trusted identities fixed when the
account was flagged, then clears the flag (flag time and trusted-identity snapshot
cleared, the failure count reset). Trusted third-party identities stay bound; the
re-verified devices stay recorded. An unbound Apple identity is revoked at Apple as in
BR-ID-28 (编排 D10-513), with the external call outside the transaction: inside the
phone-change transaction the binding row is deleted and a revocation job is written to
the outbox (with retries; the job carries the refresh token only as the stored cipher
copied before the row is deleted, never in plaintext, and decrypts it at call time as the
deletion flow does); after commit the job calls Apple's revocation. A failed
revocation is only retried and alerted on; it never rolls the phone change back. A nickname-only
edit, and a phone edit of an account without the flag, neither unbind nor clear anything.
The audit record of such a save also lists the providers unbound and that the flag was
cleared; the response shape is unchanged (no unbind count in it).

server's internal order for the same time), page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200, above

post.summary: Record a device of the user as re-verified without changing the phone (旧号加验)
post.description:
Permission point `user.phone_change` (04 §11.2, 编辑会员信息; the nearest existing point —
04 §11.2 has no point of its own for this operation; 编排 D10-513); lacking it is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up:
totp tier, as that point (without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`). BR-WDR-01 细则「旧手机号被二次放号时的提现加验」, 清除标记只走人工: the
user contacts customer service, who checks the identity in the WeCom conversation by hand;
when the phone number is not changed, the console may only record the device the user
names as a re-verified device. The "pending re-verification" flag, its time and the trusted
identities stay as they are (nothing here clears the flag; clearing only happens with a
phone change through PATCH /admin/v1/users/{user_id}/profile, BR-ID-44).
Body: `device_id` (the X-Device-Id of the device, as registered by POST /v1/devices; the
console picks it from GET /admin/v1/users/{user_id}/devices) and `reason` (required; trimmed
of leading and trailing white space it must be 1–200 characters: what was checked in the
WeCom conversation).
Checks, in this order, first hit wins: permission (10403) → step-up (10003) → body (20001
with `data.fields` naming the field; an empty reason after trimming is
`data.fields=[reason]`) → an unknown `user_id`, or one of another app, is 20001 with
`data.fields=[user_id]` → a `device_id` that is unknown, of another app, revoked, or not a
device of this user (no session of this user, revoked sessions included, was bound to it;
D10-571 ⑨, D10-585) is 20001 with
`data.fields=[device_id]` → the account's deletion is complete is 30419 with
`data.reason=account_deleted`, and an account in deletion (users.status deleting) is 30419
with `data.reason=account_deleting` and `data.stage` (D10-585) → the account carries no pending
re-verification flag is
30419 with `data.reason=reverify_not_pending` (a device recorded before a later flag would
bypass that flag; 代理补全的默认, as D10-246).
Effect: one reverified_devices row (app, user, the device's device_hash, source admin) is
written; a device already recorded (by the user's own re-verification or an earlier
console record) is not written again and the answer has `created: false`. The failure
count of BR-WDR-01 细则「加验依据」 is not touched. Every request that passes the permission,
step-up and body checks writes one audit record (action user_reverified_device_add: admin,
reason, user_id, device_id, result code; never the device_hash), refusals included. No
Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): a retry is naturally idempotent (`created: false`, one more
audit record).

post.summary: Correct a user's real-name data (name and ID number) on the user's behalf (audited)
post.description:
Permission point `user.realname_fix` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). The user contacts customer service in a
WeCom (企业微信) conversation; the agent checks the user's identity there by hand (no
system verification flow, 2026-10-05) and submits the corrected `name` and `id_no`
(18-digit resident ID number) with `reason` (1–200 characters: what was checked in the
WeCom conversation). Rules: BR-ID-25 细则「实名更正」.
Body checks first: a missing or over-long field is 20001 with `data.fields` naming it. An
unknown `user_id`, or one of another app, is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`.
Not accepted (judged before the checks below, no vendor call), first hit wins, each 30419
(08 §13.11; only in /admin/v1) with `data.reason`: the user's realname_status is not
verified (`realname_not_verified`; a user who never verified does it in the App); the
account is in the deletion flow (BR-ID-27; also refused in the cooling period): cooling or
processing is `account_deleting` with `data.stage` (the values of 10007's `data.stage`),
done is `account_deleted` without `data.stage`; the user has any withdrawal outside the
terminal set of BR-WDR-08 (`withdrawal_in_progress`; finance brings it to a terminal state
first); the account carries the "pending re-verification" flag (`reverify_pending`;
BR-WDR-01 细则「旧手机号被二次放号时的提现加验」; cleared by hand first); the id_no_hmac of
the current real name is blacklisted (`identity_blacklisted`; BR-ID-31 ID-number
dimension; passed to risk control).
Then the same order as the user's own real-name verification (POST /v1/me/realname):
20001 format of `id_no` (18 digits and check digit, `data.fields=[id_no]`) → 44001 the new
ID number is blacklisted (a console-side refusal: no risk_hits record, not an appealable
blocked request, BR-ID-36) → 30407 age (BR-ID-26) → 30405 the new id_no_hmac is verified
on another account of this app (the user's own current value does not count; that
account is never revealed) → vendor two-element verification: a mismatch is 30406 and
leaves the stored real name as it was; vendor timeout or error is 50401 / 50301 and saves
nothing. Attempts are not counted against the user's 3 per day (no 30410 here).
On a match, in one transaction that locks the user row (the same user-level lock as a
withdrawal application): withdrawals are checked again and a new non-terminal one refuses
the correction as above (30419 with `data.reason=withdrawal_in_progress`); when the old identity has a paid-out
withdrawal (PAID_API / PAID_MANUAL), the old name and ID ciphertexts, id_no_hmac and
verified_at move to the isolated store first (BR-ID-25 细则「旧身份留存」; viewing it
comes with a later contract); then the realname row's name and ID ciphertexts,
id_no_hmac, birth_date, provider and verified_at are overwritten, every bound payout
account of the user is invalidated (written to payout_account_changes; this invalidation
and the first rebinding after it are not counted in the user's monthly changes), and the
domain event `user.realname_corrected` (old and new id_no_hmac, never plaintext) is
queued in the same transaction (规划/02 §11). Minor rules follow the new birth_date.
Audit: every submission that passes the permission, step-up and body checks writes one
audit record (action user_realname_correct: admin, reason, result code, the new values
masked or their id_no_hmac, never the plaintext), refusals included; a success also
records the masked before and after values (BR-ID-33). The name and the ID number never
go into logs. The response is the user's real name as it is now, masked. No
Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): a retry after a lost response is a new submission with its
own checks, vendor call and audit record.

post.summary: Register a request for a user's personal information copy (audited, asynchronous)
post.description:
Permission point `user.data_export` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). The user asks for a copy of their
personal information in a WeCom (企业微信) conversation; the agent checks the identity
there by hand and registers the request here (BR-ID-40; 04 §6.6 users/{id}/data-exports).
Body (20001 with `data.fields` naming a missing or invalid field): `reason` (1–200
characters, including the agent's written conclusion of the identity check) and the two
channel facts the agent confirmed in the conversation, `app_login_ok` (the user can sign
in to the App) and `phone_sms_ok` (the bound phone number can receive SMS). An unknown
`user_id`, or one of another app, is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`.
Then, first hit wins:
1. Account state (BR-ID-40 细则「副本请求与注销状态」): an account whose deletion is
   processing is not accepted (30419 with `data.reason=account_deleting` and
   `data.stage=processing`), nor one whose deletion is done (30419 with
   `data.reason=account_deleted`, no `data.stage`); the cooling period is accepted as
   usual.
2. An unfinished request of the user (pending, running or ready; at most one) is returned
   instead of creating one, with `reused=true`; the channel facts of this call are not
   judged. Exception (BR-ID-40 细则「重新登记与登记人停用」): a `wecom_session` request
   not yet delivered whose registrant's admin account is disabled, or who no longer
   holds both `user.data_export` and `pii.reveal_phone`, is set to failed now and a new
   request is created as in the next point.
3. Delivery from the channel facts: both true → `in_app_sms`, which also needs a bound
   phone number (else 20001 with `data.fields=[phone_sms_ok]`); both false →
   `wecom_session` (the `reason` must say why the in-app message and the phone cannot be
   used), which needs the caller to hold `pii.reveal_phone` as well (else 10403 with
   `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`; the registrant is the only one who can
   download it); only one true → not accepted, pending legal confirmation (30419 with
   `data.reason=delivery_undecided`; BR-ID-40, 规划/06 Q-F17).
30419 is 08 §13.11's code for an assisted request the user is not accepted for now (only
in /admin/v1).
A new request starts in pending (`reused=false`). `due_at` is the end (24:00 +08:00) of
the 15th working day after the registration day (the registration day itself not counted; working days as in BR-ID-27); when the user's latest
request is failed, or a `wecom_session` one that expired without being delivered, the
new request records it in `retry_of` and keeps its `due_at` (the time limit counts from
the first registration). The copy is generated asynchronously (scope in BR-ID-40 细则
「导出范围」) into a private object-storage bucket; `expires_at` is 24 hours after
generation (BR-ID-30 ⑨). `in_app_sms`: the file is encrypted with a one-time extraction
code, an in-app message carries only an entry to the App page `DataCopy` (no link), the
code goes by SMS to the bound phone number and the request is delivered at once; the
user downloads through GET /v1/me/data-copies/{id}/download. `wecom_session`: the
request stays ready until the registrant downloads it (POST
/admin/v1/users/{user_id}/data-exports/{export_id}/download). The template codes of the
in-app message and the SMS are fixed with the implementation; the wording waits for
BR-TEXT.
Audit (BR-ID-40): every registration that passes the permission, step-up and body checks
writes one audit record (action user_data_copy_request: admin, user, reason, the two
channel facts, the result — created, reused with the returned request's id, or the
refusal code); generating and delivering write their own records. No Idempotency-Key
(04 §6.6): a retry returns the unfinished request with `reused=true`.

post.summary: Get the file of a WeCom-delivered personal information copy (registrant only, audited)
post.description:
Only for requests with delivery `wecom_session` (BR-ID-40 细则「企业微信会话交付的下载」;
04 §6.6): the copy holds the full phone number and the Agent conversations, so the caller
must hold both `user.data_export` and `pii.reveal_phone` (04 §11.2; lacking either is
10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) and every call needs a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` (else 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). Only the registrant
(`requested_by`) can download, even a super admin cannot download another account's
request: an unknown `export_id`, a request of another user or another app, an
`in_app_sms` request and another account's request are all 20001 with
`data.fields=[export_id]`. An unknown `user_id` is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`.
Only a request in status `ready` or `delivered` whose `expires_at` has not passed can be
downloaded; any other status (pending, running, failed, expired, cancelled; one past
`expires_at` answers expired even before the server has set the status) is 30417 with
`data.status` (the request's status, personal_data_copy_status; 08 §13.11 widened 30417 to
personal information copies, only in /admin/v1).
The first call (status ready, judged under a lock on the request row) generates a
one-time password, encrypts the delivery file with it and returns the password in
`password`, only in this response (never stored, never in logs or audit); the request
becomes delivered (an audit record of the delivery). Later calls sign a new link to the
same file with `password=null`. `regenerate: true` re-encrypts a new file with a new
password (returned in this response) and voids the previous file; `due_at` and
`expires_at` do not change, and after `expires_at` nothing can be regenerated (30417 with
`data.status=expired`, BR-ID-40 细则). Send the file and the password to the user in the WeCom conversation in separate
messages.
Every call is authorized again and signs a new link (as GET /admin/v1/exports/{id}/download);
`url` is valid until `url_expires_at` = min(5 minutes from now, the request's
`expires_at`). Every call that returns a link writes its own audit record (action
user_data_copy_download: admin, user, request id, regenerate; never the link or the
password) before the response is sent. The response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.
No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): a retry after a lost first response gets `password=null`,
and the registrant then calls again with `regenerate: true`.

first.summary: First download (the password is generated now)

regenerate.summary: The password was lost; re-encrypt with a new one

200.description: A freshly signed link, and the password when one was generated by this call.

Cache-Control.description: Always no-store; the signed link and the password are not cached by any proxy or the browser.

get.summary: Sub-orders of the app (filters, page by page, newest paid first)
get.description:
The order list of the console (01 F-ADM-05; 04 §6.6 orders; design/specs/admin-orders.md).
Read only, no step-up. Permission point `order.view` (04 §11.2) reads every sub-order of
the console's app. An account holding only `user.lookup` (04 §11.1: it may see the orders
of a user it looks up) may read the list only together with `user_id`, the user detail
page's orders tab (design/specs/admin-user-detail.md); without `user_id` that account gets
10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`, the same as an account holding neither
point. A super admin holds every point. Writes: manual sync (/admin/v1/order-syncs), Excel
import (/admin/v1/rights-imports), hold / unhold and assigning an unattributed order
(/admin/v1/orders/{order_id}/hold, unhold, reassign; CT-24n).

One row per sub-order (04 §3.2 orders), with its `order_id` for the detail route. Filters combine
with AND: `platform`, `platform_status`, `rebate_status`, `flag` (enum admin_order_flag:
only rows whose flag of that name is true, see the row's `flags`), `user_id` (the
attributed user; the user filter takes the user_id only: UID and phone number go through
the top-bar search GET /admin/v1/search, not this list; an unattributed order never
matches it), `q`, `paid_from` (inclusive) and `paid_to` (exclusive). `q` is trimmed of
surrounding whitespace and spaces inside are removed, then it must be 1–64 characters, else
20001 with `data.fields=[q]`; it matches exactly (no prefix or partial match) the
sub-order number (`sub_order_id`) or the parent order number (`parent_order_id`), so a
parent order number lists all its sub-orders. `paid_from` and `paid_to` are ISO 8601 times
with offset (04 §5) compared with `paid_at`; `paid_from` later than `paid_to` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[paid_from, paid_to]`, and a row without `paid_at` never matches either bound.
A `user_id` that names no user of the app, or a filter set nothing matches, is an empty
page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error. A value outside an enum is 20001 with
`data.fields` naming the parameter.

Order: `paid_at` descending (rows without `paid_at` last), then the server's internal
order for the same time. Pages with `page` (any positive integer, as AdminPage; a page past
the last one is `items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (a `page_size` above 200 is 20001, as
AdminPageSize); `total` is the count of the filter set. Amounts are integer fen. The
attributed user is shown as user_id and phone number masked 3 + 4 (BR-ID-33), never the
full number; `user` is null for an unattributed order. The Chinese names of the statuses
and flags come from the console dictionary (BR-TEXT-25 admin_dict), not from this
contract. Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: One page of sub-orders, newest paid first.

get.summary: One sub-order with its status history, commission snapshot and link records
get.description:
The order detail page (01 F-ADM-05; 04 §6.6 orders; design/specs/admin-order-detail.md).
Read only, no step-up. Permission point `order.view` (04 §11.2) reads any sub-order of the
console's app. An account holding only `user.lookup` (04 §11.1) must pass `user_id` (the
user it is looking at); without it the account gets 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`, the same as an account holding neither point. The
sub-order is named by its `order_id` (04 §3.2 orders / order_keys, the id a list row and an
order hit of GET /admin/v1/search carry; 04 §6.6 `orders/{id}`). When `user_id` is given
(by any account) and the order is attributed to another user or to nobody, the answer is
20001 with `data.fields=[order_id]`, the same as an unknown order_id or an order of another
app: unknown and not visible deliberately share one code (no probing, as GET
/admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}), so there is no 404 here.

Same fields as a list row plus the product, quantity and attribution fields of 04 §3.2
orders, `display_status` (what the user sees, derived by BR-FUND-17, not stored), `reason`,
`row_version`, `unmapped_pending_open` (derived, not stored: hold_reason UNMAPPED_STATUS
with the BR-FUND-02 pending record still open), the latest manual hold `last_hold_by`,
`last_hold_by_name`, `last_hold_note` and `last_hold_at` (from its audit record, null when
never held by hand; a system hold does not count), `status_history`, `commission_split`
and `link_logs`. Flags: `locked` is the
attribution lock orders.locked (BR-ATTR-20; the console calls it 「归属已锁定」);
`status_locked` is derived, not stored: true when rebate_status is VOID, CREDITED or
CLAWED_BACK (BR-FUND-01 细则「订单锁定（展示标记）」; the console calls it 「已锁定」). The
two are independent and may both be true. Neither has a separate time or reason in 04: the
attribution source is `user_basis`, and when the status lock began is in
`status_history`.

`status_history` lists order_status_history oldest first: `field` (platform or rebate),
`from` (null for the first value), `to`, `event` (the transition code as stored, such as
R5 of BR-FUND-01), `source` and `at`. `commission_split` is the commission snapshot
(commission_splits, BR-CALC-10: written once, null until it is generated, for instance
while the order is unattributed): amounts in fen, ratios in basis points (1/10000), the
beneficiaries with role, ratio and forfeit reason. `link_logs` lists the records of the
order's link (orders.link_id; empty when the order has no link): the 50 newest, newest
first, each with its time, event and scene only: no product, shop, promotion, user or raw
union data.

The raw union payload (union_raw_payloads, the 「原始报文」 card of the design spec) is not
returned: 04 §11 defines no permission point for it, so it stays out of this contract
until one is decided (pending). Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: The sub-order with its history, commission snapshot and link records.

post.summary: Pause the rebate of one sub-order (hold)
post.description:
The 【暂停结算】 action of the order detail page (01 F-ADM-05; 04 §6.6 `orders/{id}/hold`;
BR-FUND-06 细则「后台 hold / unhold」). Permission point `order.hold` (04 §11.2); lacking it
is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. No step-up, no Idempotency-Key.
Sets orders.hold=true and orders.hold_reason; rebate_status is not changed (BR-FUND-06).

`reason_code` (enum order_hold_reason, only RISK or CS: UNMAPPED_STATUS is set by the
system alone, BR-FUND-02) is derived from the permission points the operator holds
(BR-FUND-06 细则「后台 hold / unhold」): when it can be derived it may be left out; a value
that differs from the derived one, or no value when nothing can be derived (the operator
picks one), is 20001 with `data.fields=[reason_code]`, and so is a value outside RISK and
CS. `note` is required (1–200 characters, else 20001 with `data.fields=[note]`) and goes
into the audit record. An unknown `order_id` or an order of another app is 20001 with
`data.fields=[order_id]` (no 404, as GET /admin/v1/orders/{order_id}).

CAS: `expected_row_version` is the `row_version` GET /admin/v1/orders/{order_id} returned;
a mismatch is 20902 with `data.resource=order`. A hold the order does not accept is the
same 20902 with `data.resource=order`: the start state of R11 does not match (BR-FUND-01
R11) or the order is already held (BR-FUND-06 细则). Writes an audit record (action hold,
reason_code, note), which the detail returns as `last_hold_by`, `last_hold_by_name`,
`last_hold_note` and `last_hold_at`. The response is the order detail as it is now (same
shape as GET /admin/v1/orders/{order_id}).

200.description: The order detail as it is now (held).

post.summary: Resume the rebate of one held sub-order (unhold)
post.description:
The 【恢复结算】 action of the order detail page (01 F-ADM-05; 04 §6.6 `orders/{id}/unhold`;
BR-FUND-06 细则「后台 hold / unhold」). Permission point `order.hold` (04 §11.2); lacking it
is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. No step-up, no Idempotency-Key.
Sets orders.hold=false and clears orders.hold_reason; rebate_status is not changed.

`reason_code` is required (enum order_hold_reason, only RISK or CS; missing or another
value is 20001 with `data.fields=[reason_code]`). `note` is required (1–200 characters,
else 20001 with `data.fields=[note]`) and goes into the audit record. An unknown
`order_id` or an order of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[order_id]`.

CAS: `expected_row_version` is the `row_version` GET /admin/v1/orders/{order_id} returned;
a mismatch is 20902 with `data.resource=order`. An unhold the order does not accept is the
same 20902 with `data.resource=order`: the start state of R11 does not match (BR-FUND-01
R11), the order is not held, or it is held with UNMAPPED_STATUS while the pending record
of BR-FUND-02 is still open (未关闭; the detail's `unmapped_pending_open` is then true and
the console greys out 【恢复结算】; BR-FUND-06 细则). Writes an audit record (action unhold,
reason_code, note). The response is the order detail as it is now (same shape as GET
/admin/v1/orders/{order_id}).

200.description: The order detail as it is now (no longer held).

post.summary: Assign an unattributed sub-order to a user
post.description:
Unattributed order assignment (01 F-ADM-05; 04 §6.6 `orders/{id}/reassign`; BR-ATTR-31).
Permission point `order.assign` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier (动态码; without a valid
totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). One admin completes it alone
(ADD-05). No Idempotency-Key: only an order whose user_id is null is accepted, so a repeated
submit gets 20902.

Only an unattributed order (user_id null) is assigned; moving an already attributed order
to another user is not offered (负责人 2026-10-18; the console's 「改归属」 is editing the
member and manual adjustment). The request carries what the operator saw:
`expected_user_id` (only null) and `expected_locked` (the detail's `flags.locked`). The
server reads the order again; when its user_id is non-null (already attributed: by a sync,
a claim or another assignment before this submit) or `locked` differs from
`expected_locked`, the answer is 20902 with `data.resource=order_attribution` and nothing
is changed.

`user_id` is the target user. An unknown `order_id` or an order of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[order_id]`; an unknown `user_id` (or a user of another app) is 20001
with `data.fields=[user_id]` (no 404, as GET /admin/v1/orders/{order_id}). A target user
who cannot be the attribution target (BR-ATTR-31 细则「改归属的目标用户」) is 20001 with
`data.fields=[user_id]` and `data.reason`: target_banned (risk state banned),
target_deleting (deletion in progress) or target_deleted (deleted). A frozen user (冻结)
is accepted. `reason` is required (5–200 characters, BR-ATTR-20 ③; else 20001 with
`data.fields=[reason]`) and goes into the audit record. The response is the order detail
as it is now (same shape as GET /admin/v1/orders/{order_id}).

example.reason: 用户提供购买截图，核实后指派

200.description: The order detail as it is now (attributed to the target user).

post.summary: Request a manual order sync (by time window or by order numbers)
post.description:
Manual sync of the order console (01 F-ORD-10; 04 §6.6 `order-syncs`). Permission point
`order.view` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`.
No step-up, no Idempotency-Key. The body takes exactly one of two forms:

- by time window: `platform`, `from`, `to` (ISO 8601 with offset) and an optional
  `status_filter`, the order status filter the platform's order query supports, only a
  value registered for that platform in `specs/union/<platform>.md` (an unregistered value
  is 20001 with `data.fields=[status_filter]`). The window is cut into deliveries of the
  window limit of 02 §7.1; `from` may not be earlier than the farthest look-back
  (回扫) range of that platform (02 §7.1 table), which GET /admin/v1/order-syncs/limits
  returns as `earliest_from`. `from` not before `to`, or a `from` earlier than
  `earliest_from`, is 20001 with `data.fields=[from, to]` or `[from]`.
- by order numbers: `platform` and `order_nos` (sub-order numbers, 1–50, 01 F-ORD-10;
  `max_order_nos` of the limits); 【同步此单】 of the order detail sends just one. A platform
  whose `max_order_nos` is 0 has no sync by order number: `order_nos` for it is 20001 with
  `data.fields=[order_nos]`.

Mixing the two forms, a value outside an enum, or more than 50 order numbers is 20001 with
`data.fields` naming the field. Identity (app, requesting admin) comes from the admin token,
never from the body.

The request is recorded in order_sync_requests and runs asynchronously: `status` is queued
(排队) until a worker takes it, then running (执行), done or failed. While a request with
the same filter (the deduplication key of 02 §7.1, which carries a digest of the filter)
is queued or running, submitting it again creates nothing new and returns the original
request with `reused=true` (复用). When the sync stream of the chosen platform depends on
the site owner's (站长) authorization and that stream is paused (BR-ID-24 ④), the request is
refused with 30156 and `data.platform`.

orderNos.summary: One order from the order detail (【同步此单】)

200.description: The sync request, new or the one already queued or running with the same filter.

statusFilterInvalid.summary: 20001 status_filter not registered for the platform

tooEarly.summary: 20001 from earlier than the platform's earliest_from

streamPaused.summary: 30156 the platform's sync stream is paused while the site owner's authorization is suspended

value.msg: 该平台的站长授权已暂停，暂不能手动同步

get.description:
What the manual sync form may send, per platform (01 F-ORD-10; 04 §6.6 `order-syncs`).
Permission point `order.view` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. One item per platform the console can sync:
`earliest_from` is the earliest window start the platform's look-back range allows now
(computed from the farthest look-back range of 02 §7.1, so it moves with the clock; not a

post.summary: Import a rights, punishment or channel order Excel file
post.description:
Excel import of the order console (01 F-ORD-10; 04 §6.6 `rights-imports`; 04 §3.2
rights_imports). Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Only `kind=channel` (渠道单) writes the blocklist
and therefore also needs permission point `risk.blocklist` and step-up of the totp tier
(动态码; without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`;
BR-ATTR-26 细则「渠道单导入」); rights and punish need neither. The handler checks this
condition, so the operation carries no operation-level step-up marker. No Idempotency-Key.

`multipart/form-data` with the parts:
- `kind` (enum rights_import_kind): rights (维权单, by sub-order number: every row must
  have one, a row with only the parent order number is not expanded and is a row failure
  sub_order_no_missing), punish (违规单, by sub-order number, written as
  `order_rights.type=PUNISH`) or channel (渠道单, by relation_id, with `union_account_id`
  required);
- `platform` (enum platform);
- for rights and punish only: optional `time_basis` (paid or received, the payment or
  receipt time of 01 F-ORD-10) with optional `from` and `to` (ISO 8601 with offset). A
  window needs both ends and `time_basis`: `from` or `to` without `time_basis` is 20001
  with `data.fields=[time_basis]`, and one end without the other names the missing `from`
  or `to`. Without a window no row is filtered and `time_basis` may be omitted; sent alone
  it is accepted and ignored (04 §6.6; 08 BR-FUND-06). Rows outside the window are
  skipped (`skipped_rows`; row rules in BR-FUND-06 细则「维权导入任务」). With
  `kind=channel` any of the three is 20001 with `data.fields` naming it;
- `file`: the xlsx file, at most 10,000 rows (1 万行).

A file that is not xlsx or cannot be read is 20001 with `data.fields=[file]`, and so is a
file over 10,000 rows; a `kind` outside the enum is 20001 with `data.fields=[kind]`; a
request body above the global limit is HTTP 413 with 20001 and `data.fields=[body]`. The
columns of each Excel type follow the union's official export template (registered by
the contract line from docs-mirror, marked 待验证 until tested).

The import runs asynchronously: the response carries `import_id` and `status` (queued).
Rows go one by one through the settlement command into order_rights (BR-FUND-01), channel
rows through the risk port into the blocklist (BR-ATTR-26 ②). A row error is a row failure
in the result (GET /admin/v1/rights-imports/{import_id}), never an error of this request.
Rows already imported under the deduplication key of BR-FUND-06 count as
`duplicate_rows`; uploading the same file again creates a new import task (新任务), whose
already imported rows count as `duplicate_rows`.

200.description: The import task, queued.

413.description: Request body above the global limit (20001 with data.fields=[body]).

fileInvalid.summary: 20001 not an xlsx file, unreadable, or over 10,000 rows

timeBasisMissing.summary: 20001 from / to without time_basis, or time_basis with kind=channel

fromInvalid.summary: 20001 from missing while to is sent, not a time, or sent with kind=channel

toInvalid.summary: 20001 to missing while from is sent, not a time, or sent with kind=channel

get.summary: Order claims to review (filters, page by page, a count per claim status)
get.description:
The claim review list (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims; BR-ATTR-18). Read only, no step-up.
Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) reads every claim of the console's app. An
account holding only `user.lookup` (04 §11.1: it may see the claims of a user it looks up)
may read the list only together with `user_id`, the user detail page's claims tab
(design/specs/admin-user-detail.md); without `user_id` that account gets 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`, the same as an account holding neither point. A
super admin holds every point. Approving and rejecting stay with `order.claim` alone
(CT-24l).

Filters combine with AND: `platform`, `evidence_level` (enum claim_evidence_level, the
claim's level, that is its weakest child order), `status` (enum claim_status), `user_id`
(the applicant; the user filter takes the user_id only: UID and phone number go through
the top-bar search GET /admin/v1/search, not this list) and `q`. `q` is trimmed of
surrounding whitespace and spaces inside are removed, then it must be 1–64 characters,
else 20001 with `data.fields=[q]`; it matches exactly (no prefix or partial match) a
claim_id (the display number of a claim is its claim_id; there is no separate claim
number), the order number as submitted, or the number of one of the claim's child
orders. A `user_id` that names no user of the app, or a filter set nothing matches, is an
empty page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error; `counts` still follows its own rule
below (every filter except `status`), so a `status` nothing matches leaves the other
counts as they are (a user with 3 approved claims and none rejected, read with
`status=rejected`: `items=[]`, `total=0`, `counts.approved=3`), and every count is 0 only
when the filters other than `status` match nothing. A value outside an enum is 20001 with
`data.fields` naming the parameter.

Order: claims with status `auto_matched` first (BR-ATTR-18: kept at the top for the
reviewer), then every other claim; within each group `submitted_at` descending, then the
server's internal order for the same time. Pages with `page` (any positive integer, as
AdminPage; a page past the last one is `items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (a `page_size`
above 200 is 20001, as AdminPageSize). `counts` has one entry per claim_status value (0 included), counted with
every filter of the request except `status`, so the console's status tabs show what each
tab would hold; `total` is the count of the page's own filter set. The applicant is shown
as user_id and phone number masked 3 + 4 (BR-ID-33), never the full number. Reading does
not write an audit record.

200.description: One page of claims, auto_matched first, then newest submitted first, with a count per status.

get.summary: One claim with its child orders and the evidence view
get.description:
The claim review page (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims; BR-ATTR-18). Read only, no step-up.
Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) reads any claim of the console's app. An account
holding only `user.lookup` (04 §11.1) must pass `user_id` (the user it is looking at);
without it the account gets 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`, the same as
an account holding neither point. When `user_id` is given (by any account) and the claim's
applicant is another user, the answer is 20001 with `data.fields=[claim_id]`, the same as
an unknown claim_id or a claim of another app (no probing). The display number of a claim
is its claim_id.

Same fields as a list row plus `reason` (the note of the latest approval or rejection,
claims.reason, null before any; every note is kept in the audit log) and `items`, one per child order (claim_items): its own evidence level (BR-ATTR-18 counts per
child order, for the applicant only), the decision (null while pending), the reject reason
(enum claim_reject_reason, set with a rejection only), when and by whom it was decided
(`decided_by` null for a decision made by the system: a NOT_IN_POOL or ORDER_INVALID
rejection or a cancellation after attribution by sync), the reviewer's display name
(`decided_by_name`: admin_users.display_name, the username when that is empty, null when
`decided_by` is null or the account is gone), the `row_version` that the approve and
reject operations take as `expected_row_version` (CT-24l), `matches` and `evidence_links`.
`matches` compares, field by field, what the user submitted with what the union reported
for that child order (enum admin_claim_match_field: order number, payment date; for a
pre-sale order the union side is the date the deposit was paid), values as strings in the
contract's formats, with the server's verdict in `matched`. `evidence_links` lists the
link records that count as the child order's evidence (BR-ATTR-18: the applicant's own
convert and open records with result_code 0 inside the window before the child order's
attribution time, newest first), each with its time and scene only: no product, shop,
promotion or raw union data. It is empty for evidence `none`. Reading does not write an
audit record.

200.description: The claim with its child orders.

post.summary: Approve one child order of a claim (returns the whole claim after the review)
post.description:
Approves one child order (claim_items) of a claim (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims; BR-ATTR-18,
BR-ATTR-20). Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) only: an account holding only
`user.lookup`, or neither, gets 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied` (a super
admin holds every point). No step-up. No Idempotency-Key: the console's writes rely on the
CAS below (04 §6.6). One child order per call; there is no batch approval.

Request: `expected_row_version` is the child order's `row_version` from
GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}. `reason` is required for approval and rejection alike,
5–200 characters (the console may prefill 「证据核实一致」); after trimming surrounding
whitespace it must still have at least 5 characters, else 20001 with
`data.fields=[reason]`; it is stored trimmed. An unknown claim_id or a claim of another
app → 20001 with `data.fields=[claim_id]`; an unknown item_id, or one that belongs to
another claim → 20001 with `data.fields=[item_id]`. A child order that is already decided
(approved, rejected or cancelled, by a reviewer or by the system, such as sync
attribution closing it under BR-ATTR-16), or whose `row_version` is no longer
`expected_row_version` → 20902 with `data.resource=claim_item`, nothing changed; the
console refreshes and shows the result.

Approval runs in one transaction under BR-ATTR-20: it takes
pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(platform, sub_order_id)), the same lock as sync and admin
assignment (BR-ATTR-01), re-reads the order with SELECT … FOR UPDATE, and then checks in
this order (BR-ATTR-20 ② before ③):
- The order's user_id is no longer empty (attributed by sync, by another claim or by an
  admin assignment): the order is not written and no commission snapshot is made; the
  child order is closed as BR-ATTR-16 says, `cancelled` when that user_id is the
  applicant, else `rejected` with `reject_reason=NOT_IN_POOL`. This is not an error: the
  answer is 200 with the claim as it is after closing. Signal (no extra field): the
  reviewed child order's `decision` in the response. A request to approve whose child
  order comes back `cancelled`, or `rejected` with NOT_IN_POOL, was closed this way, and
  the console tells the reviewer 「订单已被自动归属」.
- Else the order's rebate_status is VOID: the system rejects the child order with
  `reject_reason=ORDER_INVALID` (BR-ATTR-18; a claim never takes a VOID order,
  BR-ATTR-17 ④c, BR-ATTR-20 ③), again 200 with the claim; the order is not written.
- Else the child order becomes `approved` and the order is attributed to the applicant
  as BR-ATTR-20 ③ says: user_id, user_basis=claim, locked=true, platform_status
  unchanged, rebate_status out of UNATTRIBUTED by BR-FUND-01 R3, the commission snapshot
  under the conditions of BR-ATTR-01 ⑥, order_status_history with source=claim, the
  domain event claim.resolved queued in the same transaction, and source backfill
  (BR-ATTR-15). Every other pending child order of the same sub order (in claims of other
  applicants) is rejected with NOT_IN_POOL in the same transaction (BR-ATTR-18: the first
  approval wins).
A child order closed by the system (`cancelled`, NOT_IN_POOL, ORDER_INVALID) has
`decided_by` null, as GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id} describes; an approval has the
reviewer.

In every outcome the child order's `row_version` goes up by 1 and `decided_at` is set,
`reason` is written to claims.reason (the latest note, shown as the claim's `reason`) and
to the audit log together with the operator and the outcome; child orders have no note
of their own. When every child order of the claim is decided, the claim's `status` is
summarized (BR-ATTR-18: any approved → approved; else any rejected → rejected; else
cancelled); while one is pending it stays as it is. The applicant is told the result by
in-app message and push (BR-ATTR-18). The response is the whole claim after the review,
the same shape as GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}.

post.summary: Reject one child order of a claim with a reviewer reject reason (returns the whole claim)
post.description:
Rejects one child order (claim_items) of a claim (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims;
BR-ATTR-18). Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) only: an account holding only
`user.lookup`, or neither, gets 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. No
step-up and no Idempotency-Key (CAS, 04 §6.6). One child order per call; there is no
batch rejection.

Request: `expected_row_version`, `reason` and the errors for them, for an unknown
claim_id or item_id and for a decided or changed child order are the same as
POST /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}/items/{item_id}/approve (`reason` 5–200 characters,
else 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`; 20902 with `data.resource=claim_item`).
`reject_reason` takes only the six codes a reviewer may choose (BR-ATTR-18): NO_EVIDENCE,
EXPIRED_CLICK (the applicant only has records of the same product older than 360 hours),
NOT_TRACKED, OTHER_TLJ, FRAUD, OTHER. NOT_IN_POOL and ORDER_INVALID are set by the system
only; sending one of them, or any other value → 20001 with `data.fields=[reject_reason]`.

Rejection runs in one transaction: it takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(platform,
sub_order_id)), the same lock as approval, sync and admin assignment (BR-ATTR-01), re-reads
the order with SELECT … FOR UPDATE, and then:
- The order's rebate_status is VOID: the system rejects the child order with
  `reject_reason=ORDER_INVALID` (BR-ATTR-18: an order already void at review is rejected
  by the system, whether the reviewer pressed approve or reject; approval does the same),
  not with the reviewer's `reject_reason`, and `decided_by` is null (a system decision,
  as in approval). This is not an error: the answer is 200 with the claim. Signal (no
  extra field): the reviewed child order comes back with `reject_reason=ORDER_INVALID`.
- Else the child order becomes `rejected` with that `reject_reason` and `decided_by` the
  reviewer.
In both outcomes `decided_at` is set and `row_version` goes up by 1; the order itself is
not written. `reason` is written to claims.reason (the latest note) and to the audit log
with the operator, the reject reason the reviewer chose and the outcome (including
ORDER_INVALID). When every child order is decided the claim's `status` is
summarized as BR-ATTR-18 says (any approved → approved; else any rejected → rejected;
else cancelled); while one is pending it stays as it is. The applicant is told the result
by in-app message and push (BR-ATTR-18). The response is the whole claim after the
review, the same shape as GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}.
