Permission point `notify.channels` (04 §11.2; no `content.fund_terms`, also for a fund
code); lacking it is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier
on every call (without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`). 「测试发送 / 重新测试」 of the pending registration of the code ×
variant (`variant`, `default` when absent), whatever its current test result. Order of
checks, the first hit is returned: permission, step-up → `code` not a template code of the
app → 20001 with `data.fields=[code]` → `variant` not a variant of the code → 20001 with
`data.fields=[variant]` → body (20001 with `data.fields` naming the field; a `sample` key
that is not one of the variant's variables → `data.fields=[sample]`) → no pending
registration → 20001 with `data.fields=[variant]` → `row_version` differs from the code's
current one → 20902 without data → the account has no verify phone (BR-ID-45) → 10003
with `data.tier=totp` and `data.reason=verify_phone_missing` (no step-up prompt: register
the verify phone first; this operation is the only one that returns it, D10-339 ⑤),
nothing sent or saved. Otherwise one SMS goes synchronously to the operator's own verify
phone with the pending signature and template CODE, filled with `sample` (variables not
given take the server's built-in sample value), and the result replaces the pending
registration's `test` (raising `row_version`, re-checked when it is written): accepted →
200 with `test.status=accepted`; the provider rejects it (including a wrong signature or
template CODE) or errors → 50301; times out or the outcome is unknown → 50401; on both
`test.status=failed` is saved and the active registration stays in force. The test SMS
counts against the provider's rate limits for that phone. Writes an audit record (action
notify_sms_test: code, variant, the masked verify phone and the result). The response is
the code's item as GET returns it now and the masked phone of the test send. No
Idempotency-Key: a retry sends again.

post.description:
Permission point `notify.channels` (04 §11.2), and for a fund code also
`content.fund_terms` (D10-339 ③); lacking either is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier on every call (without a valid
totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). 「启用新配置」, from the test
result dialog or later from the code's edit drawer (D10-339 ①). Order of checks, the
first hit is returned: permission, step-up → `code` not a template code of the app →
20001 with `data.fields=[code]` → a fund code without `content.fund_terms` → 10403 →
`variant` not a variant of the code → 20001 with `data.fields=[variant]` → body (20001
with `data.fields` naming the field) → no pending registration, or its `test.status` is
not `accepted` (failed, or not sent for want of a verify phone) → 20001 with
`data.fields=[variant]` (only a registration whose test the provider accepted can be
enabled, BR-TEXT-20 细则) → `row_version` differs from the code's current one → 20902
without data. The gate is the pending registration's accepted test, which already
satisfied BR-TEXT-20's test send to a verify phone: the enabling operator needs no verify
phone of their own and nothing is sent here (orchestrator ruling D10-342 ②; permission
and step-up as above). Otherwise the pending registration becomes the active one of the code ×
variant (replacing the earlier active one; `enabled_at` = now), the pending one is
cleared and `row_version` goes up by 1; from then on that code × variant is sent with it
(for `SMS_CODE` the deployment fallback no longer applies). When this makes `sms_ready`
true, a code in `sms_state=enabled_not_ready` starts sending SMS (`enabled`); a code
whose SMS is off stays off until switched on. Writes an audit record (action
notify_sms_enable: code, variant, the active registration before and after, whether it is
a fund code). The response is the code's item as GET returns it now. No Idempotency-Key.

put.summary: Save the version settings of one platform and channel (created when absent)
put.description:
Permission point `content.app_version` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up by request (04 §11.2, BR-ID-34): when the
saved `min_supported_version` is higher than before (none before — no row yet, or null —
counts as higher), a totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` is required (without one → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`; operation `content.app_version.raise_min_supported_version`); any other
save needs no step-up. Only ios, android and harmony are saved here (h5 and admin rows are
read-only). The request replaces the whole row. CAS: `expected_row_version` is the
row's `row_version` as the console showed it, null when this platform and channel has no
row yet (the save creates it); a mismatch — including null while a row exists, or a
number while none exists — → 20902 with `data.resource=app_version`, refresh and retry
(04 §6.6). A save adds 1 to `row_version` (a new row starts at 0). A failed check is
20001 with `data.fields` naming the field: a malformed value; a channel that does not go
with the platform (`[channel]`); a store key (`default_store`, `store_listings[].store`,
`confirmed_stores[]`) not among the keys specs/app-stores.yaml has filled in for this
platform and channel (while none is filled in, only the format is checked); a store
repeated in `store_listings`; and the check before saving of BR-ID-01 细则
「【去更新】打开哪家商店与保存前的核对」, run when this save raises
`min_supported_version`, changes a store's `listed_version` or changes `default_store`
(reordering `store_listings` alone does not run it): the default store not meeting it →
the fields of this save that changed among `min_supported_version`, `default_store` and
`store_listings`; another store whose `listed_version` is below `min_supported_version`
and not listed in `confirmed_stores` → `[confirmed_stores]` (stores listed there without
need are ignored). The server never lowers anything on the operator's behalf, and does
not check the order of the three version numbers against each other. Writes an audit
record with the values before and after and the stores confirmed. The response is the row
as saved. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6; the CAS keeps a retry from saving twice).

200.description: The row as saved.

Permission point `config.risk` (04 §11.2; read only, no step-up); lacking it is 10403 with

the rules are seeded with B1-03, BR-ID-36), ordered by `scene`, then `rule_id`; not paged
and not filtered (04 §6.6 risk-rules). Each row holds the fields of 04 §6.6 only:
`rule_id`, `scene` (the code the rule seed registered; no closed list in this contract),
`name` (display name), `risk_action` (BR-ID-36), `status` (enabled or disabled),

`threshold_keys` names the configuration items that hold the rule's thresholds (an empty
array for a rule without one). Their current values and allowed ranges are not returned
here: they are read and changed only through /admin/v1/config-items (PUT
/admin/v1/config-items/{key}, these keys being registered under `config.risk`), so each
value has one write path. `version` is what POST /admin/v1/risk-rules/{rule_id}/enable and
…/disable take as `expected_version`.

get.summary: Appeals to handle (filters, page by page, four counts)
get.description:
The risk appeal console (风控申诉页; 04 §6.6 appeals; BR-ID-36). Permission point
`risk.appeal` (04 §11.2; read only, no step-up); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied` (a super admin holds every point). Every appeal of
the console's app: the account and order appeals users submitted in the app (POST
/v1/me/appeals) and the appeals customer service registered here (POST
/admin/v1/appeals), blocked_request appeals included.

Filters combine with AND: `status` (enum appeal_status), `overdue`, `target_type` (enum
appeal_target_type) and `q`. `overdue=true` keeps only the appeals still processing whose
`deadline_at` has passed (the internal time limit of BR-ID-36: the 3rd working day 24:00
+08:00 after submission); `overdue=false` or absent filters nothing. `q` is trimmed of
surrounding whitespace, then it must be 1–64 characters, else 20001 with
`data.fields=[q]`; it matches exactly (no prefix or partial match) an appeal_id (the
display number of an appeal is its appeal_id; there is no separate appeal number) or the
UID (user_id) of the appellant. A filter set nothing matches is an empty page
(`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error. A value outside an enum is 20001 with
`data.fields` naming the parameter.

Order: `created_at` descending, then the server's internal order for the same time. Pages
with `page` (any positive integer, as AdminPage; a page past the last one is
`items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (above 200 is 20001, as AdminPageSize). `counts` has
four numbers, each counted with every filter of the request except `status` and
`overdue`, so the console's four tabs show what each would hold: `processing` (status
processing), `overdue` (processing and past `deadline_at`; a part of `processing`),
`closed` (upheld or revoked) and `all`; `total` is the count of the page's own filter
set.

The appellant is shown as user_id and phone number masked 3 + 4 (BR-ID-33), never the
full number (only through POST /admin/v1/users/{user_id}/reveal, 04 §11.1); `user` is
null for a register-type blocked_request appeal (no account). Reading does not write an
audit record.

200.description: One page of appeals, newest submitted first, with the four counts.

post.summary: Register an appeal on a person's behalf (代登记申诉)
post.description:
Customer service registers an appeal for someone who contacted them through WeCom (企业
微信): a request blocked with 44001 (the only kind possible for someone without an
account), or an account or order appeal (04 §6.6 appeals, §11.2 `risk.appeal`; BR-ID-36,
细则「被拦截请求申诉」). Permission point `risk.appeal`; lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. No step-up. The appeal is written through the
risk module's appeal service (single writer risk, 04 §3.2 appeals); this operation only
calls it.

Request: `target_type` (enum appeal_target_type) and `target_id` — for account the
user's UID (user_id), for order the order_id, for blocked_request the
`blocked_request_id` found with GET /admin/v1/blocked-requests. `content` is the
person's own statement (用户陈述). `reason` is the registration note (登记原因说明),
required: after trimming surrounding whitespace 1–200 characters, else 20001 with
`data.fields=[reason]`; it goes to the audit log only, is never shown to the user and has
no column of its own (04 §3.2 appeals). `user_id` is optional: the appellant is always
derived by the server from the target — account: `target_id`; order: the order's
user_id; blocked_request: the blocked request's user_id (none for the register type) —
and a `user_id` that differs from it (any value for a register-type blocked request
included) is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]` (编排裁定 D10-158).

Who may appeal is the same as POST /v1/me/appeals (04 §6.1, BR-ID-36): account — a user
whose risk_state is banned or frozen (or appealing, which has a processing appeal, see
below); order — an order whose rebate risk control voided (BR-ATTR-26); blocked_request
— a request blocked with 44001 (a risk_hits row with ref_type blocked_request). An
unknown target, a target of another app and a target that cannot be appealed are all
20001 with `data.fields=[target_id]`.

Order of checks, as for POST /v1/me/appeals: 20001 (body, target and user_id checks) → a
processing appeal on the same target returns that original appeal and creates nothing
(for a register-type blocked request also an appeal processing on the same related
phone number, BR-ID-36 细则「被拦截请求申诉」), never 30418 → the appeal count for the
target used up (BR-ID-36 细则「维持后再申诉」; registered appeals count the same as
appeals submitted in the app) → 30418 → create the appeal.

A new appeal is processing, with source admin, the caller as registrant, `deadline_at`
by BR-ID-36 and no handler. An account appeal sets the user's risk_state to appealing
and records prev_risk_state; an order appeal only marks the order as under appeal
(appeal_pending, 拍板第二批 OPS-07); a blocked_request appeal changes no risk_state and
sends no in-app message (BR-ID-36). Creating writes an audit record (action
appeal_register, with the target, the appellant and the registration note); returning
the processing appeal writes none. The response is the appeal as GET
/admin/v1/appeals/{appeal_id} returns it, new or the processing one already on the
target. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): a repeated request finds the processing appeal and
returns it.

get.summary: One appeal with its risk hit records and the blocked request
get.description:
The appeal detail page (04 §6.6 appeals; BR-ID-36). Permission point `risk.appeal` (read
only, no step-up); lacking it is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. An
unknown appeal_id or an appeal of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[appeal_id]`.

Same fields as a list row plus: `content` (the appellant's statement), `risk_state` (the
appellant's risk state now, enum risk_state; null without an account), `source` (enum
appeal_source: submitted in the app, or registered in the console) with the registrant
(`registered_by`, `registered_by_name`; null for an app submission), `claimed_at` (the
last claim; null when never claimed and after closing), `closed_at`, `row_version` (the
`expected_row_version` of claim and resolve), `revoke_permission`, `blocked_request` and
`risk_hits`.

`revoke_permission` is the permission point that revoking this appeal needs on top of
`risk.appeal` (04 §11.2 `risk.appeal`, BR-ID-36 细则「被拦截请求申诉」权限): `risk.ban` for
an account appeal against a ban (prev_risk_state banned), `risk.freeze` for one against
a freeze (frozen), `risk.blocklist` for a blocked_request appeal whose request a
blocklist entry blocked (cause blocklist; 编排裁定 D10-154); null otherwise (order
appeals, blocked requests blocked by another rule). When it is not null revoking also
needs a totp-tier step-up; upholding never needs either.

`blocked_request` is the blocked request (request type, the amount for a withdrawal,
when it was blocked and the reason category) for a blocked_request appeal, null
otherwise. `risk_hits` lists the related risk_hits rows newest first, at most 50: for an
account appeal the user's, for an order appeal those whose object is the order, for a
blocked_request appeal those of the blocked request; each with its time, rule, action
and related object number only. Never the hit dimension's value, its HMAC or the rule's
conditions (BR-ID-36). The phone number is masked as in the list (BR-ID-33). Reading
does not write an audit record.

post.summary: Claim an appeal (marks the caller as its handler; not exclusive)
post.description:
Marks the caller as the handler of a processing appeal (认领; 04 §6.6 appeals). Only a
mark, not a lock (编排裁定 D10-158): another account holding `risk.appeal` can claim it
again, which rewrites the handler and `claimed_at`, and any account holding
`risk.appeal` can resolve the appeal whether or not it claimed it; there is no release
or transfer. Permission point `risk.appeal`; lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. No step-up. Written through the risk module's
appeal service (04 §3.2 appeals, writer risk).

Request: `expected_row_version` is the appeal's `row_version` from GET
/admin/v1/appeals/{appeal_id}. An unknown appeal_id or an appeal of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[appeal_id]`. An appeal that is no longer processing, or whose
`row_version` is not `expected_row_version`, is 20902 with `data.resource=appeal`,
nothing changed; the console refreshes. Otherwise `handler_id` becomes the caller,
`claimed_at` the server's current time and `row_version` goes up by 1, also when the
caller already was the handler. Writes an audit record (action appeal_claim, the handler
before and after). The response is the appeal as GET /admin/v1/appeals/{appeal_id}
returns it. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6; the CAS keeps a retry from claiming twice).

post.summary: Close an appeal as upheld or revoked (结案)
post.description:
Closes a processing appeal (04 §6.6 appeals; BR-ID-36, BR-ID-31). Any account holding
`risk.appeal` can resolve it, claimed or not (编排裁定 D10-158). Written through the risk
module's appeal service in one transaction (04 §3.2 appeals, writer risk); this
operation only calls it.

Request: `decision` (`upheld` 维持 or `revoked` 撤销), `note` and `expected_row_version`
(the appeal's `row_version`). `note` is the internal note (结案内部说明), required: after
trimming surrounding whitespace 1–200 characters, else 20001 with `data.fields=[note]`;
it goes to the audit log only and is never shown to the user (04 §3.2 appeals: no
column).

Permission and step-up (04 §11.2 `risk.appeal`; BR-ID-36 细则「被拦截请求申诉」权限): the
permission point `risk.appeal` always. Revoking an account appeal against a ban
(prev_risk_state banned) also needs `risk.ban`, against a freeze (frozen) also
`risk.freeze`, and revoking a blocked_request appeal whose request a blocklist entry
blocked (cause blocklist) also `risk.blocklist` (编排裁定 D10-154); each of these three
also needs a totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token`. Upholding, revoking an order appeal and
revoking a blocked_request appeal blocked by another rule (cause rule) need `risk.appeal`
only and no step-up. GET /admin/v1/appeals/{appeal_id} returns the extra point as
`revoke_permission`.

Order of checks: `risk.appeal` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
body (20001 with `data.fields` naming the field) → an unknown appeal_id or an appeal of
another app (20001 with `data.fields=[appeal_id]`) → an appeal no longer processing, or
whose `row_version` is not `expected_row_version` (20902 with `data.resource=appeal`,
nothing changed; refresh) → for `revoked`, the extra permission point (10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → its step-up (10003 with `data.tier=totp`).

Effects, in one transaction: `status` becomes the decision, `closed_at` the server's
current time, `handler_id` the caller (the resolver, whoever claimed it), `claimed_at`
null, and `row_version` goes up by 1.
- account: upheld → risk_state goes back to prev_risk_state; revoked → risk_state
  normal, and revoking a ban unbans the user as BR-ID-31 says (the union bindings blocked
  for ban come back as PUT /admin/v1/users/{user_id}/risk-state `unban` describes; taobao
  ones become invalid).
- order: upheld → the order is no longer under appeal and stays voided; revoked → the
  settlement module creates the appeal restore difference (appeal_restore, BR-FUND-22,
  拍板第二批 FUND-14) from the domain event below.
- blocked_request: no risk_state changes. Revoked with cause blocklist → the blocklist
  entries that caused the block are removed in the same operation (BR-ID-31, written to
  the audit log; 编排裁定 D10-154); revoked with cause rule → the one-time pass of BR-ID-36
  细则「被拦截请求申诉」 (kept and checked inside the server, not part of this contract).
  The system never resubmits the blocked request: the person submits it again. Upheld →
  the block stays.
Both decisions queue the domain event appeal.resolved {app_id, appeal_id, user_id,
target_type, target_id, status, need_reauth} in the same transaction (04 §3.2 appeals;
编排裁定 D10-141). need_reauth (boolean, BR-TEXT-23) is true only when an account appeal
revoked against a ban leaves the user's Taobao union binding invalid after the unban
(BR-ID-31), false for every other resolution; the notification module then sends the in-app message APPEAL_RESULT for
account and order appeals (BR-TEXT-23). blocked_request appeals get no in-app message
or SMS: customer service tells the person in the WeCom conversation (BR-ID-36). Writes
an audit record (action appeal_resolve, with the decision, the note and the appeal's
state before and after). The response is the appeal as GET
/admin/v1/appeals/{appeal_id} returns it after closing. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6; the
CAS keeps a retry from closing twice).

get.summary: Find requests blocked with 44001 (by full phone number, UID or blocked request id)
get.description:
The lookup of the 【代登记申诉】 dialog (04 §6.6 appeals「被拦请求查找」, §11.2
`risk.appeal`; BR-ID-36 细则「被拦截请求申诉」登记). Permission point `risk.appeal` (read
only, no step-up); lacking it is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`.

Exactly one of `phone`, `user_id` and `blocked_request_id`; none or more than one is
20001 with `data.fields=[phone, user_id, blocked_request_id]`. `phone` is the full
number, normalised as in BR-ID-05 细则「手机号规范化」 (not a mainland mobile number → 20001
with `data.fields=[phone]` and `data.reason=phone_invalid`); it matches the blocked
requests whose related phone number (stored as HMAC only, BR-ID-33) is that number, and
the blocked requests of the account that number belongs to now. `user_id` (the UID)
matches that user's blocked requests. `blocked_request_id` matches that one request
exactly; it is the only way to find a request without a phone number (a third-party
first login blocked at the same-device register limit, BR-ID-05). Only requests of the
console's app blocked with 44001 (risk_hits rows with ref_type blocked_request) are
listed; nothing found is an empty page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error.

Each item: `blocked_request_id` (拦截请求编号, the risk_hits ref_id shown in the 44001
dialog), `request_type` (enum blocked_request_type), `phone_masked` (3 + 4, BR-ID-33;
null when the request has no related phone number), `blocked_at`, the reason category
(`cause`, enum blocked_request_cause, and `blocklist_dimension`, enum
blocklist_dimension, for cause blocklist, else null; never the value that was hit or the
rule's conditions), `amount_fen` (the amount asked for, request type withdraw only, else
null) and `processing_appeal_id` (the appeal processing on this request, or for a
register-type request on the same related phone number; null when none: the console
then opens that appeal instead of registering a new one). Order: `blocked_at`
descending, then the server's internal order; pages with `page` and `page_size` ≤ 200
(as AdminPage, AdminPageSize).

A lookup by `phone` that finds at least one request writes an audit record (action
blocked_request_lookup, the masked number and the number found), as a lookup by full
phone number under `user.lookup` does (04 §6.6); lookups by `user_id` or
`blocked_request_id`, and a phone lookup that finds nothing, write none.

get.summary: Pay orders of the app (filters, page by page, newest first)
get.description:
The pay order list of the console (04 §6.6 pay-orders; BR-PAY-02, BR-PAY-05). Read only,
no step-up. Permission point `pay.view` (04 §11.2). One row per pay order (04 §3.2
pay_orders) with its `pay_order_id` for the detail route, the refunded total
`refunded_fen` (refunds do not change the pay order status; 「已退款」「部分退款」 are
derived from it, BR-PAY-06 ③), `closing` (the close flow is running) and `needs_manual`
(automatic closing stopped at expire_at + `pay.close_wait_minutes`; settled through POST
/admin/v1/pay-orders/{pay_order_id}/resolve, BR-PAY-05 ③).

Filters combine with AND: `status`, `pay_channel`, `biz_type`, `user_id` (our user),
`out_trade_no` (exact match), `needs_manual`, `created_from` (inclusive) and `created_to`
(exclusive), both ISO 8601 with offset compared with `created_at`; `created_from` later
than `created_to` is 20001 with `data.fields=[created_from, created_to]`. A value outside
an enum is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the parameter; a filter set nothing matches is
an empty page. Order: `created_at` descending. Pages with `page` and `page_size` ≤ 200;
`total` is the count of the filter set. Amounts are integer fen. No channel-side user
identifier is returned (BR-PAY-08 ④). Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: One page of pay orders, newest first.

get.summary: One pay order with its refunds and recent channel request summaries
get.description:
The pay order detail of the console (04 §6.6 pay-orders). Read only, no step-up.
Permission point `pay.view` (04 §11.2). `pay_order` is the same shape as a list row;
`refunds` lists the pay order's refunds (pay_refunds with target_type pay_order), newest
first; `query_attempts` summarizes the 20 newest channel requests recorded for the pay
order and its refunds (pay_query_attempts, newest first), each with its `kind`, `result`
and time `at` only: the request and response bodies are never returned. An unknown
`pay_order_id`, or a pay order of another app, is 20001 with
`data.fields=[pay_order_id]` (no 404). Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: The pay order with its refunds and request summaries.

post.summary: Settle a needs_manual pay order by querying the channel now
post.description:
The manual settlement of BR-PAY-05 ③ (【立即查询】). Permission point `pay.resolve`
(04 §11.2). Step-up: totp tier (04 §11.2, BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`. Only for a pay order with
`needs_manual=true` in status PENDING: the body is fixed (`expected_status=PENDING`,
`action=query_and_settle`); the console sends no channel result, status or evidence of
its own. A pay order that is no longer PENDING, or whose `needs_manual` is false, is 20902
with `data.resource=pay_order` (refresh the detail). An unknown `pay_order_id` is 20001
with `data.fields=[pay_order_id]`.

The server queries the channel now (a pay_query_attempts row of kind query) and settles by
the channel's answer: paid → PO2, the pay order becomes PAID (with the PAY_RECEIPT
posting and the business opening of BR-PAY-04); closed, or not exist under the condition
of BR-PAY-05 ② (past expire_at + `pay.close_grace_minutes` and still not exist on this
query) → PO3, the pay order becomes CLOSED; anything else (unknown, not paid yet, the
query failed, or not exist before that time) → no change, the pay order stays PENDING
with `needs_manual=true` and the answer says so. The evidence of the settlement is the
query response the server recorded (kept with the attempt, not returned); `channel_result`
is its summary. Every call is written to the audit log (action pay_order_resolve, with the
query result and the status before and after), the unchanged outcome included. No
Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): a repeated call queries again and settles by CAS on
`expected_status`.

200.description: The pay order after the query, with the summary of the channel's answer.

paid.summary: The channel says paid; the pay order became PAID

unknown.summary: The channel's answer is unknown; the pay order stays PENDING

post.summary: Refund a PAID pay order through its original channel
post.description:
The original-route refund of BR-PAY-06. Permission point `pay.refund` (04 §11.2); no
step-up (owner decision 2026-10-05). The refund goes back through the pay order's own channel to
the account it was paid from: the body carries only `amount_fen` (positive integer fen), the required
`reason_code` (enum pay_refund_reason) and an optional `note` (at most 200 characters);
target, channel, refund number and status are fixed by the server. The pay order must be
PAID, else 20902 with `data.resource=pay_order`. An amount that would exceed the
refundable amount (the successful plus processing refunds of the pay order, plus this
one, above its `amount_fen`, BR-PAY-06 ③) is 20001 with `data.fields=[amount_fen]`. An
unknown `pay_order_id` is 20001 with `data.fields=[pay_order_id]`.

`Idempotency-Key` is required (BR-PAY-06 ②): the same key with the same body gives the
same refund (one pay_refunds row and one `out_refund_no`, generated at creation and never
changed) and returns the first result; the same key with another body is 20901; the same
key while the first request is still running is 40901. The answer is the refund as
created, normally PROCESSING; its result comes later from the channel (BR-PAY-06 ④⑤) and
is read back through GET /admin/v1/pay-refunds/{pay_refund_id}. The pay order status does
not change; `refunded_fen` grows when the refund succeeds. Every refund is written to the
audit log (action pay_refund_create, with the operator, amount and reason code).

get.summary: Pay anomalies (money received without a payable pay order), page by page
get.description:
The pay anomaly list of the console (BR-PAY-05 ④; 04 §3.2 pay_anomalies). Read only, no
step-up. Permission point `pay.view` (04 §11.2). One row per anomaly: money the channel
shows as received for a CLOSED pay order, or for a merchant order number that names no pay
order of ours (`pay_order_id` is then null; `out_trade_no` is null when the channel gave

the refundable remainder is `amount_fen` minus the successful and processing refunds. The
evidence kept with the anomaly is not returned. Filters: `pay_channel`; a value outside the

post.summary: Refund a pay anomaly through its original channel
post.description:
The original-route refund of a pay anomaly (BR-PAY-05 ④, BR-PAY-06). Permission point
`pay.refund` (04 §11.2); no step-up (owner decision 2026-10-05). Same body and rules as
POST /admin/v1/pay-orders/{pay_order_id}/refunds: `amount_fen` (positive integer fen),
the required `reason_code` (enum pay_refund_reason) and an optional `note`; the refund
goes back the way the money came, with target, channel, refund number and status fixed by
the server. An amount that would exceed the refundable amount (the successful plus
processing refunds of the anomaly, plus this one, above its received `amount_fen`,
BR-PAY-06 ③) is 20001 with `data.fields=[amount_fen]`; an unknown `pay_anomaly_id` is
20001 with `data.fields=[pay_anomaly_id]`.

`Idempotency-Key` is required (BR-PAY-06 ②): same key and body → the same refund and the
first result; same key with another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901.
The answer is the refund as created, normally PROCESSING; read its result through GET
/admin/v1/pay-refunds/{pay_refund_id}. Every refund is written to the audit log (action
pay_refund_create, with the operator, amount and reason code).

get.summary: Pay reconciliation differences (source R4), page by page
get.description:
The pay reconciliation page of the console (BR-PAY-07; 04 §6.6 pay-orders). Read only, no
step-up. Permission point `pay.view` (04 §11.2). Only recon_diffs of source R4 (收款对账,
the daily T+1 check of the channel's bills by out_trade_no and out_refund_no) are listed,
of type `pay_mismatch` or `pay_anomaly`; differences of R1–R3 are not here. Each row has its
`recon_diff_id`, `period` (the bill date), what it refers to (`ref_type`, `ref_id`), the
three amounts in fen (`expected_fen` ours, `actual_fen` the channel's, `diff_fen`) and its
`status`. Filters combine with AND: `type` and `status`; a value outside an enum is 20001
with `data.fields` naming the parameter. Order: `created_at` descending. Pages with `page`
and `page_size` ≤ 200. Handling a difference (query again and settle, register an anomaly
and refund, or close after checking) is not part of this operation. Reading does not write
an audit record.

200.description: One page of R4 reconciliation differences, newest first.

get.summary: Reconciliation differences of sources R1–R3, page by page
get.description:
The 差错单 list of the reconciliation console (01 F-ADM-08; 04 §3.2 recon_diffs;
design/specs/admin-recon.md §4). Read only, no step-up. Permission point: any of
`fund.recon` or `fund.view` (04 §11.1, §11.2). Only recon_diffs of source R1 (联盟对账),
R2 (通道对账) or R3 (内部日终与月末核对) are listed; source R4 (收款对账: `pay_mismatch`,
`pay_anomaly`) stays in GET /admin/v1/pay-recon-diffs and is not a value of `source` here.
Each row has its `recon_diff_id`, `source`, `type`, `period`, what it refers to
(`ref_type`, `ref_id`), the three amounts in fen (`expected_fen`, `actual_fen`, `diff_fen`),
its `status`, `created_at` and `closed_at`. Filters combine with AND: `type`, `source`,
`status`, `ref_id` (exact match), `period_from` and `period_to` (both inclusive, compared
with `period` as strings, so a YYYY-MM period sorts before the days of its month); a
value outside an enum or pattern is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the parameter, and
`period_from` greater than `period_to` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[period_from, period_to]`. Order: `created_at` descending (then
`recon_diff_id` descending). Pages with `page` (as AdminPage; a page past the last one is
`items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (above 200 is 20001, as AdminPageSize); `total` is the
count of the filter set. No user phone number or other personal data is returned.
Handling a difference (close, appeal restore, balance recalculation, write-off) is not
part of this operation. Reading does not write an audit record.

post.summary: Close a reconciliation difference of source R1–R3 without further handling (结案)
post.description:
Closes a 差错单 as 「已关闭（不处理）」 with a required reason (01 F-ADM-08; 04 §3.2
recon_diffs, withdraw_holds; BR-FUND-19, BR-FUND-22; design/specs/admin-recon.md §4).
Permission point `fund.recon` (04 §11.2; `fund.view` alone is not enough); no step-up
(04 §11.2, design/specs/admin-recon.md §5).

Request: `reason`, required: after trimming surrounding whitespace 1–200 characters, else
20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`. Only a difference of source R1, R2 or R3 whose `status`
is `open` or `processing` can be closed. `outcome`, optional (enum
admin_recon_diff_outcome, 编排裁定 D10-447 ②, D10-506): the structured conclusion of a
月结账单金额不一致 difference, `union` 以联盟为准 or `ours` 以我方为准; a value outside the
enum is 20001 with `data.fields=[outcome]`. It has a meaning for
`type=settle_amount_mismatch` (source R1) only: any other type or source is refused, see
the order of checks.

What the conclusion does (BR-FUND-04 ④, its 校验结果 table and 例 2; D10-506): the
conclusion is bound to the amounts of the difference. `outcome=union` counts as matched
in the monthly consistency check only when the current snapshot `base_fen` equals this
difference's `expected_fen` and B_settle equals its `actual_fen`; the order then goes on
to a supplement batch. Otherwise the conclusion does not apply and the check compares
the amounts as usual: when they do not match it opens a new settle_amount_mismatch
difference, the old one stays closed and the order stays WAITING. The new difference's
`ref_id` carries an amount fingerprint, `{order_key}#AMT#{base_fen}:{b_settle_fen}` (the
current snapshot `base_fen` and B_settle), because recon_diffs is unique on (app_id, type,
period, ref_id) and the bill's `{order_key}` row is taken: a bill has at most one
difference for the same amount state. It appears in the list and detail like any other
(the `ref_id` filter is an exact match, so it needs the full value) and can be closed
with its own `outcome`. The conclusion the check reads is that of the order's difference
whose `ref_id` is `{order_key}` or starts with `{order_key}#AMT#` and whose amounts equal
the current ones. Without `outcome` there is no structured conclusion: the check
compares the amounts as needed, which can only hold back more, never pay more
(D10-447 ①). `ours` does not count as matched either. The `closed` status by itself is
not a conclusion, and the free-text `reason` is never parsed for one. The conclusion
cannot be changed: a closed difference answers 20902 to any further close.

Until B2-09h lands the route accepts `outcome` but the server neither runs the 20001
check on it nor writes it: a close carrying `outcome` still closes the difference, with
no conclusion and for good. Clients must not send `outcome` before B2-09h.

Order of checks: `fund.recon` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → body
(20001 with `data.fields=[reason]` or `data.fields=[outcome]`) → an unknown
`recon_diff_id`, a difference of another app, or one of source R4 (see
GET /admin/v1/pay-recon-diffs) is 20001 with `data.fields=[recon_diff_id]` (no 404) → a
difference already `closed`, `adjusted` or `written_off` is 20902 with
`data.resource=recon_diff`, nothing changed (refresh the detail) → from B2-09h on,
`outcome` sent for a difference that is not `type=settle_amount_mismatch` of source R1 is
20001 with `data.fields=[outcome]`, nothing changed (the same place as the guard of
write-off).

Effects, in one transaction: `status` becomes `closed`, `closed_at` and `updated_at` the
server's current time, `handler_id` the caller, and `resolution` records the trimmed
reason under the key `reason` and, from B2-09h on, `outcome` when given under the key
`outcome`. Every withdrawal hold (withdraw_holds) whose source is this
difference and that is not released yet is released in the same transaction (BR-FUND-19:
差错单关闭时解除冻结记录); `released_hold_count` is the number of holds this call released
(holds released earlier are not counted; 0 when there are none). Closing does not restore
an order, post an adjustment, write anything off or recalculate a balance cache; those
are other operations. Writes an audit record (action recon_diff_close, with the reason,
from B2-09h on `outcome` when given, and, before and after, the `status` and `released_hold_count`; no personal data). The
response is the difference as GET /admin/v1/recon-diffs/{recon_diff_id} returns it after
closing, with `released_hold_count`.

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result (the same
`released_hold_count`); same key with another body → 20901; same key while still running
→ 40901. A new key for a difference that is already closed is 20902.

200.description: The difference after closing with the number of holds released, or the first result of the same key.

post.summary: Write off an R2 late-success difference by settling the returned withdrawal as paid (核销, W11)
post.description:
The 【核销】 of design/specs/admin-recon.md §2 for one case only: the channel
reconciliation (R2, BR-WDR-23 ③) found the Alipay bill showing a transfer as successful
while the withdrawal had been returned to APPROVED as a payer-side failure (W9,
hold_reason `payer_side_after_transfer`). The difference carries that bill line; this
operation settles the original withdrawal as PAID_API on that evidence (BR-WDR-08 W11,
owner decision 2026-10-03 决-08 A), so the member is paid once, never twice.
Permission point `payout.execute` (04 §11.2; the reviewer of the withdrawal may do it,
ADD-05). Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` →
10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request: `expected_withdrawal_status`, fixed `APPROVED` (the console confirms what it
showed); `note`, optional, 1–200 characters after trimming (else 20001 with
`data.fields=[note]`), recorded under `resolution.note`. The console sends no channel
result, amount or evidence of its own: the evidence is the bill line the reconciliation
stored with the difference.

Order of checks: `payout.execute` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001) → an unknown `recon_diff_id`, a difference of another
app, or one of source R4 is 20001 with `data.fields=[recon_diff_id]` (no 404) → a
difference already `closed`, `adjusted` or `written_off` is 20902 with
`data.resource=recon_diff` → the W11 guard, each refusal 20001 with
`data.fields=[recon_diff_id]` and `data.reason`: `not_payer_side_case` (the difference
is not an R2 「支付宝成功、内部为付款方侧失败经 W9 退回」 case, for example a duplicate payout
or a missing withdrawal, which go to adjustment instead); `writeoff_disabled` (the
switch `payout.proven_success_writeoff.enabled` is off, BR-WDR-17: W11 is not enabled,
handle it as a difference plus adjustment); `withdrawal_not_returned` (the withdrawal is
APPROVED but not held as `payer_side_after_transfer`); `transfer_attempts_mismatch` (the
withdrawal does not have exactly one transfer attempt, or that attempt is not a definite
failure); `amount_mismatch` (the bill line's amount is not the withdrawal's `net_fen`).
A withdrawal that is no longer APPROVED (rejected, executed again, or settled meanwhile)
is 20902 with `data.resource=withdrawal` (BR-WDR-08: the transition is a compare-and-set;
refresh the detail), nothing changed.

Effects, in one transaction: the withdrawal moves APPROVED → PAID_API (W11, event
CHANNEL_SUCCESS_PROVEN; `paid_at` the bill line's time when it carries one, else 00:00
+08:00 of the bill day — never the time of the write-off (orchestrator ruling D10-431: a
later R2 run and the BR-WDR-21 tax quarter go by the day the channel paid);
`channel_order_id` from the bill line; the payer-side hold is cleared; the operator is
recorded as the executor) and the success voucher
`wd:{withdrawal_id}:PAID` (WITHDRAW_PAID, WITHDRAW_FEE, TAX_WITHHOLD; BR-WDR-09) is
posted against the member's frozen balance — the only money movement, and the same one
W5 would have written. The difference's `status` becomes `written_off`, `closed_at` and
`updated_at` the server's current time, `handler_id` the caller, and `resolution` keeps
its keys and adds `w11` (the withdrawal id, `paid_at` and the operator) and the trimmed
`note` when given. Every withdrawal hold whose source is this difference and that is not
released yet is released in the same transaction (the difference is handled, as for the
close; BR-FUND-19); `released_hold_count` as POST .../close. Writes an audit record
(action recon_diff_write_off, with the withdrawal id, `released_hold_count` and, before
and after, the statuses of the difference and the withdrawal; no personal data) and
publishes the withdrawal change to the wallet. The attempt record of W11 (kind `query`,
result `success`, the bill line as its evidence; BR-WDR-08 W11) is appended by the payout
process from a task queued in this same transaction (D10-428), so it shows in
GET /admin/v1/withdrawals/{withdrawal_id} shortly after, not necessarily in the response.
Nothing else changes: no adjustment, no order restore, no balance recalculation, and
`payout.queue_paused` stays as it is (BR-WDR-17). A terminal withdrawal is never touched
(BR-WDR-23).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a
header and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

post.summary: Handle an account-appeal restore difference by paying the member back (申诉恢复处理, ADMIN_RESTORE)
post.description:
The ADMIN_RESTORE of BR-FUND-22 ③ (拍板第二批 FUND-14; 编排裁定 D10-468 ①): an account (ban)
appeal was revoked, and the shares of the member forfeited for `banned` during the ban
(BR-CALC-13) and kept as platform revenue are paid back. The difference is the
`appeal_restore` the system registered when the appeal closed; the list and the detail are
GET /admin/v1/recon-diffs and GET /admin/v1/recon-diffs/{recon_diff_id}. Permission point
`order.restore` (04 §11.2; one person can complete it, ADD-05). Step-up: totp tier
(BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request: `note`, optional, 1–200 characters after trimming (else 20001 with
`data.fields=[note]`), recorded under `resolution.note`; the body is `{}` without it. The
console sends no amount. `expected_fen` of the difference is for display only: what is
paid is calculated by the server when this operation runs, and may differ from it.

Order of checks: `order.restore` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001) → an unknown `recon_diff_id`, a difference of another app,
or one of source R4 is 20001 with `data.fields=[recon_diff_id]` (no 404) → a difference
already `adjusted`, `written_off` or `closed` is 20902 with `data.resource=recon_diff` →
a difference that is not an account-appeal restore (its `type` is not `appeal_restore`,
or its `resolution.reason_code` is not `APPEAL_RESTORE`, or it has no `user_id` or
`shares` there) is 20001 with `data.fields=[recon_diff_id]` and
`data.reason=restore_not_supported`. That covers `platform_restore` and the order-appeal
R12 and R13 of BR-FUND-22, which are not handled by this operation → the member has been
deleted: 20001 with `data.fields=[recon_diff_id]` and `data.reason=restore_user_deleted`;
the difference is ended with POST .../close instead (D10-469 ①, default filled in by the
agent).

Effects, in one transaction, for each role listed in `resolution.shares` (BR-FUND-22 ③):
an `active` beneficiary event is appended for the member's role, so that later adjustments
of the order count the re-split share as owed (the appeal-restore exception of BR-CALC-09).
The member's entitlement for the role is recalculated from the order's `booked_base_fen`
and the commission snapshot, and its difference from what is already booked for the role
(net as in BR-FUND-08) is posted as ADMIN_ADJUST (sub_type RESTORE, debit
COMMISSION_REVENUE, credit USER_BALANCE.available) with uniq_key
`{order_key}:{user_id}:{role}:RESTORE:{recon_diff_id}`. A difference ≤ 0 posts nothing and
pays 0 for the role: a negative one is not taken back, and the difference is still
handled (D10-469 ③, default filled in by the agent). A member banned again by a later
round is still paid (D10-469 ②, default filled in by the agent). The exception, which
takes precedence over D10-469 ②: for a member identified as under 18, a promotion role
(`share`, `direct` or `indirect`) is not paid: instead of an `active` event a `forfeited`
event with `forfeit_reason=minor` is appended, and the role counts 0; the role `self` is
paid as usual (D10-482). Whether a role is forfeited at all is decided by one reading:
start from `beneficiaries[].initial_status`, take the latest event by `event_seq`, and
only a latest `forfeited` counts (D10-481). The `status` of the
difference becomes `adjusted`, `closed_at` and `updated_at` the server's current time,
`handler_id` the caller, and `resolution` keeps its keys and adds `restore` (the amount
paid for each role, the total, the operator and the time) and the trimmed `note` when
given. `expected_fen`, `actual_fen` and `diff_fen` stay as registered. Writes an audit
record (action recon_diff_restore, with the `user_id`, the `order_key`, the amount paid
for each role, `restored_fen` (0 when nothing was posted) and, before and after, the
`status`; no personal data). `restored_fen` in the response is the total paid by this
call. Nothing else changes: the order's `rebate_status` is not touched, and no withdrawal
hold is released (an `appeal_restore` difference carries none, BR-FUND-19).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result (the same
`restored_fen`); same key with another body → 20901; same key while still running →
40901. A new key for a difference that is already `adjusted` is 20902. The step-up token
is a header and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

post.summary: Submit a manual adjustment or a whole-form reversal, effective in one step (提交并生效)
post.description:
The only way a person adjusts a member's balance (BR-FUND-24; 04 §3.2 admin_adjustments;
design/specs/admin-adjustments.md 新建抽屉, 红冲对话框, and the 【调整余额】 of the user detail).
One submission saves and approves at once: there is no 保存待批 and no 撤回, and the form
is born APPROVED with `reviewed_by` equal to `created_by` (BR-FUND-24 细则「后台入口」, owner
2026-10-18 ②; ADD-05). Permission point `fund.adjust` (04 §11.2). Step-up: sms tier
(BR-ID-34): without a valid sms-tier `X-Step-Up-Token`, a totp-tier token included → 10003
with `data.tier=sms`; an account without a registered verify phone also gets
`data.reason=verify_phone_missing`.

Request, one of two closed shapes (AdminAdjustmentCreateRequest):

- A new adjustment: `user_id`; `direction`; `amount_fen`, integer fen > 0, no upper limit
  (BR-FUND-24 ④); `reason_code`, one of RECON_FIX, PAYOUT_RECOVERY or OTHER. RESTORE comes
  only from a difference (BR-FUND-22) and ACCOUNT_CLOSED only from the system (BR-FUND-24
  ⑧), so neither can be chosen: 20001 at the schema. `refs`, the linked documents, at
  most 10, without duplicates (`data.fields=[refs]`); `note`, the internal explanation,
  at most 500 characters and not blank after trimming (blank → `data.fields=[note]`),
  required for OTHER (`data.fields=[note]`); `contra_subject` with `contra_platform`, see
  below.
- A reversal: `reverses_adjust_id` and `note`, the reason for the reversal, required, as
  above. The request carries no direction, amount, reason code, refs or subject: the
  server takes them from the original (opposite direction, the original `amount_fen`,
  whole form only, the same `reason_code`, `contra_subject` and `contra_platform`), and
  any of those fields in the request is 20001 at the schema (BR-FUND-24 细则「红冲只按原单整笔」).
  To correct +500 to +50: reverse the whole +500, then submit a new +50.

What `data.fields` lists depends on where the body is refused. The schema comes first and
reports both shapes: a body that fits neither shape (a `reason_code` of RESTORE or
ACCOUNT_CLOSED, a `note` over 500 characters, more than 10 `refs`, an `amount_fen` of 0, a
value outside an enum, a missing required field, a field of the other shape) is 20001
with `data.fields` listing what fails in each of the two shapes, usually fields of the
other shape too, plus `body`; it does not single out the field at fault. Every
`data.fields` naming one field in this description is a check the service makes after the
body has fit one shape.

Linked documents by reason code (BR-FUND-24 ②③), all refused as 20001 with
`data.fields=[refs]`: RECON_FIX needs at least one `recon_diff`. PAYOUT_RECOVERY needs at
least one `recon_diff` and exactly one `withdrawal`. OTHER needs at least one document of
any type, or none at all when `note` is the 客服处理说明 that stands in for it (③; `note`
is required for OTHER either way). `ref_id` is `recon_diffs.id`, `withdrawals.id`, the
`order_key` of a sub-order, or `deletion_requests.id`.

Contra subject (BR-FUND-24 ⑥; specs/ledger-rules.md §6, whitelist pending the finance
confirmation): for RECON_FIX and OTHER the operator chooses `contra_subject` from
COMMISSION_REVENUE, UNION_RECEIVABLE, BAD_DEBT or MKT_EXPENSE (missing → 20001 with
`data.fields=[contra_subject]`, another value fails at the schema); `contra_platform` is
required exactly for UNION_RECEIVABLE (else `data.fields=[contra_platform]`). For
PAYOUT_RECOVERY both are refused (20001 on the field): the server takes the cash subject
from the withdrawal's channel (CASH_ALIPAY, CASH_WECHAT or CASH_BANK).

The route schema runs first (D10-590 ⑥, as every console route): a malformed body is 20001
before any of the checks below, with or without `fund.adjust`, and writes no audit record.
Order of checks: `fund.adjust` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`; the
refusal writes an audit record, action adjustment_denied, BR-FUND-24 例（无权限）) → step-up
(10003) → body (20001: the schema, then the checks above) → an unknown `user_id` or one of
another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`; an unknown `reverses_adjust_id` or one
of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[reverses_adjust_id]`; a `ref_id` that names
nothing of the app, a `recon_diff` of source R4 (a 收款对账 difference never leads to a
balance adjustment, BR-PAY-07; see AdminReconDiffIdPath), or a `withdrawal` or
`account_deletion` of another member, is 20001 with `data.fields=[refs]` and
`data.reason=adjust_ref_invalid` → an original already reversed
is 20902 with `data.resource=admin_adjustment` (a form can be reversed once, BR-FUND-16;
the console refreshes and shows 已红冲; the unique constraint on `reverses_adjust_id`
answers the same under a race) → the guards, each refusal 20001: an original that is not
APPROVED, or that is itself a reversal, with `data.fields=[reverses_adjust_id]` and
`data.reason=reverse_not_allowed`; a member already deleted with the field of the request
(`user_id` or `reverses_adjust_id`) and `data.reason=adjust_user_deleted`; a member in
deletion (users.status deleting) takes no new manual form, only the reversal of an approved
ACCOUNT_CLOSED form (D10-590 ④), anything else 20001 with the field of the request and
`data.reason=adjust_user_deleted`.

Effects, in one transaction under the member's balance lock: the balance is read again
and the form (`status=APPROVED`) and its ADMIN_ADJUST voucher (sub_type = `reason_code`)
are written, an increase debiting the contra subject and crediting
USER_BALANCE.available, a decrease the other way round. The voucher uniq_key is
`ADJ:{adjust_id}`, and `ADJ:{original adjust_id}:REVERSE` for a reversal, posted with the
reversal templates of specs/ledger-rules.md §5. A decrease, a reversal included, may take
`available` below 0 (BR-FUND-24 ⑤, BR-FUND-10); `frozen` is never written. Linking a
difference does not change its status: it is closed through its own operations. Writes an
audit record (action adjustment_create or adjustment_reverse, with the `adjust_id`, the
`user_id`, the direction, amount and reason code, `available` before and after and, for
a reversal, the original; no personal data). What the member sees (one ADMIN_ADJUST line
in the balance history, the in-app message on a decrease; BR-FUND-24 ⑦, BR-TEXT-19) is not
part of this response.

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a header
and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.
