get.description:
One form of the 调账单 tab (01 F-ADM-08; 04 §3.2 admin_adjustments;
design/specs/admin-adjustments.md 批准对话框, 红冲对话框). Read only, no step-up. Permission
point: any of `fund.adjust` or `fund.view` (04 §11.1, §11.2). `adjustment` is the list
row, next to it `balance_preview`: what executing the form now would do to `available` (BR-FUND-24
④). Only two kinds of form have one: a PENDING form, whose amount is the current
`available` (0 when `available` is not above 0, see POST .../approve), and an APPROVED
form that is not a reversal, has not been reversed and whose member is not deleted,
previewing its reversal. Every other form has `balance_preview=null`, so also an APPROVED
form of a deleted member, whose reversal POST /admin/v1/adjustments refuses with
`adjust_user_deleted`: the available balance before and after an executed form is read
from its voucher, and is not kept on the form. The preview is a reading, not
a promise: approving and reversing read the balance again in their own transaction. An
unknown `adjust_id` or a form of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[adjust_id]` (no
404). Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: The adjustment with its balance preview.

post.summary: Approve a system-prefilled ACCOUNT_CLOSED form; the amount is taken at approval
post.description:
The 【批准并短信验证】 of the 批准对话框 (BR-FUND-24 ①⑧, BR-ID-28;
design/specs/admin-adjustments.md). Only a PENDING form can be approved, and the only
PENDING forms are the ACCOUNT_CLOSED decreases the system prefills when a deletion reaches
processing: a form a person submits is APPROVED from the start. Permission point
`fund.adjust` (04 §11.2). Step-up: sms tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid sms-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token`, a totp-tier token included → 10003 with `data.tier=sms`; an account
without a registered verify phone also gets `data.reason=verify_phone_missing`.

Request: an empty object. The console sends no amount: `amount_fen` is the member's
`available` when this operation runs, which may differ from the preview.

Order of checks: `fund.adjust` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → step-up
(10003) → body (20001) → an unknown `adjust_id` or a form of another app is 20001 with
`data.fields=[adjust_id]` (no 404) → a form that is no longer PENDING is 20902 with
`data.resource=admin_adjustment` (refresh) → the balance is read again: `available` not
above 0 is 20001 with `data.fields=[adjust_id]` and `data.reason=adjust_no_balance`,
nothing is written and the form stays PENDING (the amount of a form must be above 0; the
operator rejects it instead).

Effects, in one transaction under the member's balance lock: `amount_fen` becomes the
current `available`, the voucher ADMIN_ADJUST / ACCOUNT_CLOSED with uniq_key
`ADJ:{adjust_id}` debits USER_BALANCE.available and credits COMMISSION_REVENUE (BR-FUND-24
⑥), the form becomes APPROVED with `reviewed_by` the caller and `reviewed_at`,
`voucher_id` set. No in-app message is sent to a deleted member (BR-FUND-24 ⑧). Writes an
audit record (action adjustment_approve, with the `adjust_id`, the `user_id`, the amount
and `available` before and after; no personal data).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a header
and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: The approved form with the available balance before and after, or the first result of the same key.

post.summary: Reject a system-prefilled ACCOUNT_CLOSED form with a required reason
post.description:
The 【驳回】 of the 批准对话框 (BR-FUND-24 ① and 细则「驳回与撤回不需二次验证」;
design/specs/admin-adjustments.md). Only a PENDING form can be rejected, which means a
system-prefilled ACCOUNT_CLOSED form (see POST .../approve). Permission point `fund.adjust`
(04 §11.2). No step-up of either tier: only approval needs one.

Request: `reason`, required: after trimming surrounding whitespace 1–200 characters, else
20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`.

Order of checks: `fund.adjust` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → body
(20001) → an unknown `adjust_id` or a form of another app is 20001 with
`data.fields=[adjust_id]` (no 404) → a form that is no longer PENDING is 20902 with
`data.resource=admin_adjustment` (refresh).

Effects, in one transaction: the form becomes REJECTED, `reject_note` the trimmed reason,
`reviewed_by` the caller and `reviewed_at`; `amount_fen` stays null. No voucher, and no
balance moves. Writes an audit record (action adjustment_reject, with the `adjust_id`,
the `user_id` and the reason; no personal data). The deletion does not go back: its
closing gate stays pending with a warning, and the next accounting day the deletion
processing prefills a new ACCOUNT_CLOSED form while none is PENDING (D10-590 ③).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901.

example.reason: 预填金额与核对结果不一致，次日按系统补建的新单处理

200.description: The rejected form, or the first result of the same key.

adjustment.reject_note: 预填金额与核对结果不一致，次日按系统补建的新单处理

get.summary: Bad-debt write-off candidates of the app, page by page, newest first
get.description:
The 坏账核销 tab of the 调账与核销 console (01 F-ADM-08; 04 §3.2 bad_debt_writeoffs;
BR-FUND-12; design/specs/admin-adjustments.md §2). Read only, no step-up. Permission point:
any of `fund.writeoff` or `fund.view` (04 §11.1, §11.2). Each row is
AdminBadDebtWriteoff: `candidate_fen` is the amount when the candidate was generated, for
reference only; `available_fen` and `frozen_fen` are the member's balance now;
`negative_days` is the current accounting day minus `negative_since`, derived and not
stored; `approve_blocked` is true when approving a PENDING candidate would be refused now
(the balance has frozen money and the switch `ledger.bad_debt_require_no_frozen.enabled`
is on, BR-FUND-12), so the console needs neither the switch nor its key. Filters combine
with AND: `status`, `user_id`. A value outside an enum or pattern is 20001 with
`data.fields` naming the parameter; a `user_id` that names nothing of the app is an empty
page. Order: `created_at` descending (then `id` descending). Pages with `page` (as
AdminPage; a page past the last one is `items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (above 200 is
20001, as AdminPageSize); `total` is the count of the filter set. Reading does not write
an audit record.

200.description: One page of write-off candidates, newest first.

post.summary: Approve a write-off candidate; the amount is the balance read at approval
post.description:
The 【批准核销】 of the 坏账核销 tab (BR-FUND-12; 04 §3.2 bad_debt_writeoffs;
design/specs/admin-adjustments.md 批准核销对话框). A write-off is never automatic. Permission
point `fund.writeoff` (04 §11.2; one person can complete it, ADD-05). Step-up: sms tier
(BR-ID-34): without a valid sms-tier `X-Step-Up-Token`, a totp-tier token included → 10003
with `data.tier=sms`; an account without a registered verify phone also gets
`data.reason=verify_phone_missing`.

Request: an empty object. The console sends no amount: `candidate_fen` is not used.

Order of checks: `fund.writeoff` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001) → an unknown `id` or a candidate of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[id]` (no 404) → a candidate that is no longer PENDING is 20902 with
`data.resource=bad_debt_writeoff` (refresh) → `available` and `frozen` are read again:
while the switch `ledger.bad_debt_require_no_frozen.enabled` is on (default on), `frozen`
above 0 is 20001 with `data.fields=[id]` and `data.reason=writeoff_frozen_pending`:
nothing is written and the candidate stays PENDING until the withdrawal reaches a
terminal state (BR-FUND-12, 决-11 A). With the switch off, `frozen` is not looked at.

Effects, in one transaction under the member's balance lock. `available` below 0: the
voucher BAD_DEBT_WRITEOFF with uniq_key `BADDEBT:{account_id}:{id}` debits BAD_DEBT and
credits USER_BALANCE.available by −`available` (the current amount), which brings
`available` to 0; the candidate becomes APPROVED with `approver_id` the caller,
`approved_at` and `voucher_id` set; the linked accounts (same real name, device or payee
account) get their risk mark. `available` at 0 or above: the candidate becomes CANCELLED,
with no voucher, no risk mark, `approver_id` and `approved_at` staying null, and the
answer is still 200 with `written_off_fen=0`. Writes an audit record (action
bad_debt_writeoff_approve, with the `id`, the `account_id`, the resulting status,
`written_off_fen` and `available` before and after; no personal data). Later credits
count towards the balance as usual; nothing is pursued afterwards.

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a header
and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: The candidate after approval with the amount written off (0 when it was cancelled), or the first result of the same key.

get.summary: Withdrawals of the app, page by page, newest applied first
get.description:
The review list of the withdrawal console (01 F-ADM-07; 04 §3.2 withdrawals;
design/specs/admin-withdrawals.md §1, §2, §4). Read only, no step-up. Permission point:
any of `withdraw.review` or `fund.view` (04 §11.1, §11.2); a super admin holds every
point. Each row is one withdrawal of the console's app with its `withdrawal_id` for the
detail route, its withdrawal number `out_biz_no`, the user (`user_id` and the phone number
masked 3 + 4, BR-ID-33; never the full number), `status`, `display_status` (enum
admin_withdrawal_display_status, derived from status + review_mode + hold_reason as the
BR-WDR-08 细则 table, not stored and not a new status), `review_mode`, `payout_channel`,
the four amounts in fen (`amount_fen`, `fee_fen`, `tax_fen`, `net_fen`), the
reason columns (`auto_decision` with the 转人工原因 `failed_conditions` and the 执行受阻
`execute_blocked`, `hold_reason`, `blocked_reason` for the「暂停」mark, `needs_manual`,
`reject_reason_code` with the internal `reject_note`), the review (`reviewer_id`,
`reviewed_at`), `batch_id`, the W1 `risk_flags` snapshot with `risk_flags_at`
(BR-WDR-29), `created_at` and `paid_at`. No payee account or payee name is in a row.

Filters combine with AND: `status`, `display_status` (the quick filters 待审 / 驳回 / 手动
/ 自动 of BR-WDR-08 细则 are pending_review, rejected, paid_manual and paid_auto_system or
paid_auto_review), `review_mode`, `payout_channel`, `user_id` (the user_id only; UID and
phone number lookups go through GET /admin/v1/search), `out_biz_no` (the full withdrawal
number, exact match), `amount_min_fen` and `amount_max_fen` (both inclusive, on
`amount_fen`), `created_from` (inclusive) and `created_to` (exclusive) on `created_at`
(ISO 8601 with offset, 04 §5), `hold_reason` (the W9 受阻原因), `blocked` (true = only rows
with a `blocked_reason`, false = only rows without) and `risk_flag` (only rows whose
`risk_flags` snapshot holds that code). A value outside an enum or a pattern is 20001
with `data.fields` naming the parameter; `amount_min_fen` greater than `amount_max_fen`
is 20001 with `data.fields=[amount_min_fen, amount_max_fen]`, and `created_from` later
than `created_to` is 20001 with `data.fields=[created_from, created_to]`. A `user_id` or
`out_biz_no` that names nothing of the app, or a filter set nothing matches, is an empty
page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error.

Order: `created_at` descending (then `withdrawal_id` descending). Pages with `page` (as
AdminPage; a page past the last one is `items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (above 200 is
20001, as AdminPageSize); `total` is the count of the filter set. The Chinese names of the
statuses, condition codes and risk flags come from the console dictionary (BR-TEXT-25
admin_dict), not from this contract. Writes (approve, reject, batch approve, batch and
single manual payout, automatic payout settings, cancelling a WeChat transfer), the export
and the risk flag recalculation are not part of this operation. Reading does not write an
audit record.

200.description: One page of withdrawals, newest applied first.

get.summary: One withdrawal with its amounts, batch, transfer attempts, holds, decision and risk flags
get.description:
The withdrawal detail of the console (01 F-ADM-07; 04 §3.2 withdrawals, payout_batches,
payout_batch_items, payout_attempts, withdraw_holds; design/specs/admin-withdrawal-detail.md
§1, §2, §4). Read only, no step-up. Permission point: any of `withdraw.review` or
`fund.view` (04 §11.1, §11.2). The fields of a list row, plus:
- the remaining columns of the withdrawal: `payout_method`, `review_deadline` (BR-WDR-26),
  `fail_code`, `executor_id`, `executed_at`, `execute_seq`, `manual_resolution`,
  `resolver_ids`, `manual_entry_by`, `manual_confirm_by`, `hold_at`, `channel_state`,
  `confirm_deadline` (BR-WDR-33 ⑤⑥), `channel_order_id`, `updated_at` and `row_version`;
- `payee`, the payee snapshot of the application masked only (BR-ID-33): `masked_account`,
  `masked_name` and `bank_name` (bank cards only). This operation never returns the full
  account or name, the WeChat openid or the launch data; showing them in full belongs to
  the audited reveal of the user (POST /admin/v1/users/{user_id}/reveal,
  `pii.reveal_identity`, step-up), which this task does not extend;
- `batch`: the payout batch the withdrawal is in now (payout_batches row of `batch_id`:
  `batch_id`, `kind`, `created_at`; null when `batch_id` is null), and `batch_items`, every
  payout_batch_items row of this withdrawal, oldest first (`batch_id`, `result`, `reason`,
  `moved_to_batch_id`, `at`);
- `payout_attempts`: every payout_attempts row of this withdrawal, oldest first, as a
  summary only (`attempt_id`, `kind`, `result`, `resp_code`, `resp_sub_code`, `at`); the
  channel request and response bodies are never returned;
- `holds`: the user's withdraw_holds in effect at response time (released_at null and
  hold_until null or later than the clock; BR-WDR-05, BR-FUND-19), oldest first
  (`hold_id`, `reason`, `source_ref`, `created_at`, `hold_until`).
There is no status history table for withdrawals (04 §3.2); the history of a withdrawal is
read from its stored time points (`created_at`, `auto_decision.decided_at`, `reviewed_at`
with `reviewer_id`, `executed_at` with `executor_id`, `hold_at` with `hold_reason`,
`paid_at`, `updated_at`), the batch items and the transfer attempts; admin actions are in
the audit log (GET /admin/v1/audit-logs). An unknown `withdrawal_id` or a withdrawal of
another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[withdrawal_id]` (no 404). Reading does not write
an audit record.

200.description: The withdrawal with its batch, transfer attempts, holds in effect, decision and risk flags.

post.summary: Approve the chosen withdrawals, each on its own (批量通过)
post.description:
The 【批量通过】 of the withdrawal review page; one withdrawal is a batch of one (01 F-ADM-07;
BR-WDR-10, BR-WDR-05; design/specs/admin-withdrawals.md §2, §4; ruling D10-595). Permission
point `withdraw.review`; a super admin holds every point. Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): one
valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` covers the whole request; without one → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`.

Request (AdminWithdrawalBatchApproveRequest): `withdrawal_ids`, 1 to 200 ids without
duplicates (200 is 代理补全的默认, D10-595; a duplicate is 20001 with
`data.fields=[withdrawal_ids]`).

Order of checks: the route schema comes first, before the permission and step-up checks, as
on every admin route (D10-591): a body that fails it is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the
field, also for a caller without the permission point or a token, and nothing is written.
Then `withdraw.review` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → step-up (10003) →
the duplicate check. After that the answer is 200 and each id has its own result: a
withdrawal that cannot be approved never fails the others.

Each id runs in its own transaction, in the order given: the member's locks, the
withdrawal read again, then the CAS PENDING_REVIEW → APPROVED (W2) with `reviewer_id` the
caller and `reviewed_at` the injected Clock. Results, in `items`, one per id in request
order: `approved`, or `skipped` with `reason`: `not_found` (unknown id or another app's),
`not_pending` (no longer PENDING_REVIEW, also when another request got there first),
`negative_balance` (available below 0) or `blocked` (`blocked_reason` set), the guards of W2
(BR-WDR-05 (a)). A member under a risk freeze or with an effective withdraw hold can be
approved (BR-WDR-10; those gate the application and the execution, not the review). An
unexpected failure of one id ends the request with 5xx; ids already approved stay approved,
and the same key runs the rest again (those come back `not_pending`).

Effects of each approved id: the status, `reviewer_id` and `reviewed_at`, wallet.withdrawal_changed
on the same transaction, and an audit record (action withdrawal_approve, with the
`withdrawal_id`, the status before and after and no personal data). No voucher: the money
stays frozen. Approving does not pay: execution is its own step (adminCreatePayoutBatch).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a header
and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: One result per id, or the first result of the same key.

post.summary: Record withdrawals paid outside the channel interface, each on its own (批量手动打款)
post.description:
The 【批量手动打款】 of the withdrawal page; one withdrawal is a batch of one (01 F-ADM-07;
BR-WDR-16, BR-WDR-08 W8, BR-WDR-09, BR-WDR-17; ruling D10-595). Finance has already paid the
member from a company account and records it here, so this is the way out while a channel's
transfer interface is not open. Permission point `payout.manual_entry`; a super admin holds
every point. Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): one valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` covers the
whole request; without one → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`. Entering and confirming are one
submission and one person may do both, also the reviewer (BR-WDR-16, ADD-05);
`manual_entry_by` and `manual_confirm_by` are both the caller. A separate confirmation step
is not offered.

Request (AdminWithdrawalBatchManualPaidRequest): `items`, 1 to 200 (200 is 代理补全的默认,
D10-595), each with `withdrawal_id`, `channel_order_id` (the Alipay or bank transfer serial
number, by the withdrawal's snapshot channel; 1 to 64 characters with no whitespace, so that
a stray space cannot make the same number look new, and no NUL, which the database cannot
store; compared exactly, case included),
`paid_at` (when the money was really paid) and `paid_fen` (integer fen, the amount really
paid; any integer reaches the item's own check). A withdrawal may appear only once: a duplicate `withdrawal_id` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[items]`.

Order of checks: the route schema comes first, before the permission and step-up checks, as
on every admin route (D10-591): a body that fails it is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the
field, also for a caller without the permission point or a token, and nothing is written.
Then `payout.manual_entry` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → step-up
(10003) → the duplicate check. After that the answer is 200 and each item has its own
result: an item that cannot be recorded never fails the others.

Each item runs in its own transaction, in the order given, under the member's locks and the
withdrawal's row lock, and the first check that fails is its result, in `items`, one per
request item in request order: `paid`, or `skipped` with `reason`:

- `not_found`: an unknown id, one of another app, or one that is not a UUID (which never
  reaches the database).
- `not_approved`: not APPROVED. W8 starts only there (BR-WDR-16). EXECUTE and W8 both
  require APPROVED under a CAS, and the first to commit wins, so the loser gets this and
  no money moves twice.
- `channel_not_allowed`: a wechat withdrawal; W8 is not open to it (BR-WDR-33 ⑧).
- `amount_mismatch`: `paid_fen` is not exactly the withdrawal's `net_fen` (BR-WDR-16).
- `paid_at_invalid`: `paid_at` is more than 5 minutes after the injected Clock, or before
  the withdrawal's `created_at` (代理补全的默认: no one can pay in the future or before the
  member asked, and the tax export and the watermark read this time).
- `has_transfer_attempt`: a kind=transfer attempt with result pending, success or unknown.
  That money may be out, so such a withdrawal ends through BR-WDR-15. An attempt that
  definitely failed does not stop W8.
- `query_required` or `query_success`: while the switch
  `payout.proven_success_writeoff.enabled` is on (default on), a withdrawal with
  `hold_reason=payer_side_after_transfer` is checked against its latest query, because a
  transfer the channel reported as failed may still have been paid (BR-WDR-08 W8,
  BR-WDR-17, 决-08 A). No query yet, or a latest query with an unknown result, is
  `query_required`. A latest query that succeeded is `query_success`: the channel paid, so
  this withdrawal ends through W11, and recording an offline payment too would pay twice. A
  latest query with result fail lets it through. BR-WDR-17 also allows 「订单不存在」, but that
  answer is recorded with result unknown and has no verified channel code yet (BR-WDR-22,
  BR-WDR-28), so until one is registered it is `query_required`: the safe direction. With
  the switch off this check does not run.
- `member_blocked`: a withdrawal block of the member (BR-WDR-05): risk state frozen, banned
  or appealing over either, an effective withdraw hold, available below 0, or
  `blocked_reason` set.
- `channel_order_id_taken`: `(app_id, channel_order_id)` is already on a withdrawal,
  whichever way it was paid, and also an earlier item of this request; two requests racing
  for one number are settled by the unique index, and the loser gets this.
- `identity_missing`: the member has no verified real name, so `tax_ytd` cannot be updated
  (BR-WDR-20). The money was paid and this needs a person; nothing is written.

Not checked, because they gate EXECUTE and not W8: `payout.enabled`, `payout.queue_paused`,
the channel switches (a bank_card withdrawal has only this way out while that channel is
off, BR-WDR-32 ①) and the watermark (BR-WDR-18). An unexpected failure of one item ends the
request with 5xx; items already recorded stay recorded, and the same key runs the rest again
(those come back `not_approved`).

Effects of each paid item, on one transaction: APPROVED → PAID_MANUAL (W8) with `paid_at` as
given, `channel_order_id`, `manual_entry_by` and `manual_confirm_by`, and `hold_reason` and
`hold_at` cleared; the success voucher of BR-WDR-09 with the key `wd:{withdrawal_id}:PAID`
and the cash subject of the snapshot channel (WITHDRAW:SUCCESS:CASH_ALIPAY or CASH_BANK), the
same as a success through the channel; `tax_ytd` updated (BR-WDR-20);
wallet.withdrawal_changed, which sends the member the result message (BR-WDR-26); and an
audit record (action withdrawal_manual_paid, with the `withdrawal_id`, the status before and
after, `channel_order_id`, `paid_at` and `paid_fen`; no personal data). A withdrawal on a
batch stays on it. A skipped item writes nothing: the 执行结果 column of BR-WDR-16 is rendered
from this response and is not stored, so after a reload a skipped withdrawal is an ordinary
APPROVED row again.

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with another
body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a header and not
part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: One result per item, or the first result of the same key.

get.summary: Withdrawals whose transfer result stayed unknown past the limit, waiting for a person (未知结果处置)
get.description:
The list of the 24 hour unknown disposal page (01 F-ADM-07; BR-WDR-14, BR-WDR-15; ruling
D10-625). Read only, no step-up. Permission point `payout.execute` (BR-WDR-15 sets no point
of its own); a super admin holds every point. Reading does not write an audit record.

Rows are the withdrawals of the console's app in status PAYING with `needs_manual=true`,
longest waiting first: `withdrawal_id`, `out_biz_no`, the masked `user` as in
listAdminWithdrawals (no payee account or name), `payout_channel`, `amount_fen`, `net_fen`,
`first_transfer_at` (T, the earliest kind=transfer attempt), `latest_query` (the newest
kind=query attempt, null when there is none: `result`, `at`, and what the channel answered,
`resp_code`, `resp_sub_code`, `channel_status`, `channel_order_id` and `paid_at`, each null
when absent and never the payee's account or name, so that a person can read the answer and
use it as proof), and `fail_blockers`, what
stops this withdrawal from being judged failed right now, in the order of
adminResolveUnknownPayout's checks. While the channel's 「订单不存在」 code and the bill read
are missing (D10-625) it always holds `resolve_bill_unverifiable` and
`resolve_query_unverifiable`, so the page can say why before anyone submits.

200.description: One page of the withdrawals waiting for a person.

post.summary: Ask the channel once more about a withdrawal; the answer lands later (立即查询)
post.description:
The 【立即查询】 of the disposal page (BR-WDR-15; rulings D10-595 ③, D10-596 ①, D10-625). The
channel keys live only in the payout process, so this queues one query and answers
`submitted`; the result appears as `latest_query` when the job has run, and the page refreshes
to see it. Permission point `payout.execute`; a super admin holds every point. Step-up: totp
tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.
The request has no body fields.

Order of checks: the route schema first, as on every admin route (D10-591). Then
`payout.execute` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → step-up (10003) → an
unknown `withdrawal_id` or one of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[withdrawal_id]`
(no 404) → a withdrawal that is neither of the two below is 20902 with
`data.resource=withdrawal`.

Two kinds of withdrawal can be queried: PAYING with `needs_manual=true` (automatic queries
have stopped, BR-WDR-14), and APPROVED with `hold_reason=payer_side_after_transfer`, which
has no other way to get a query recorded and needs one before W3 or W8 (BR-WDR-17, D10-596 ①).

The job asks the channel once, on the withdrawal's own out_biz_no, and only appends one
kind=query attempt. **It moves nothing:** no status change even on a success or a definite
failure, no voucher, no next query point, no second transfer (BR-WDR-14). A person ends the
withdrawal through adminResolveUnknownPayout, W3, W8 or W11. 「订单不存在」 is recorded as result
unknown until its channel code is verified (BR-WDR-22, BR-WDR-28).

Writes an audit record (action payout_query_request, with the `withdrawal_id`, the status and
no personal data) on the transaction that queues the job. `Idempotency-Key` is required:
same key and body → the first answer and no second job; same key with another body → 20901;
same key while still running → 40901. A new key queries again. The step-up token is a header
and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: The query is queued, or the first answer of the same key.

post.summary: End a withdrawal whose result stayed unknown (W10, 未知结果处置)
post.description:
The 【确认处置】 of the disposal page (BR-WDR-15, BR-WDR-08 W10, BR-WDR-09, BR-WDR-14; rulings
D10-595, D10-625, D10-626). Permission point `payout.execute`; a super admin holds every point;
one person may do it (ADD-05). Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request (AdminUnknownPayoutResolveRequest): `resolution`, `paid` or `failed`; `proof_text`,
the pasted proof, the query answer or the bill line naming this out_biz_no, 1 to 4000
characters and not blank after trimming (text only, no file upload, D10-595 ②; stored in
`proof_file` and not shown to the member). With `paid`, also `channel_order_id` (1 to 64
characters, no whitespace or NUL, compared exactly) and `paid_at` (when the channel paid).

Order of checks: the route schema first, as on every admin route (D10-591). Then
`payout.execute` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → step-up (10003) →
a blank `proof_text`, or `paid` without `channel_order_id` or `paid_at`, is 20001 with
`data.fields` naming them → an unknown `withdrawal_id` or one of another app is 20001 with
`data.fields=[withdrawal_id]` (no 404) → a withdrawal not PAYING with `needs_manual=true`, or
changed by another request, is 20902 with `data.resource=withdrawal`. A `needs_manual`
withdrawal never becomes PAID_MANUAL and is never transferred again (BR-WDR-15).

**`paid`** (the proof shows the channel succeeded): while the latest kind=query attempt has
result fail and `recon_channel` has no success line for this out_biz_no, 20001 with
`data.fields=[resolution]` and `data.reason=resolve_query_failed`: the channel said the
transfer failed and nothing contradicts it, so telling the member the money arrived could be
false, and the bill reconciliation of that day would not catch it afterwards. A later query
or a bill line lifts this; the money stays frozen meanwhile. `paid_at` more than 5 minutes
after the injected Clock, or before T, is 20001 with `data.fields=[paid_at]` and
`data.reason=resolve_paid_at_invalid`; a `channel_order_id` already on another withdrawal is
20001 with `data.fields=[channel_order_id]` and `data.reason=resolve_order_id_taken`, also
when two requests race and the unique index settles it. Otherwise, on one transaction: W10 to
PAID_API with `paid_at`, `channel_order_id`, `manual_resolution=paid`, `resolver_ids` the caller
and `proof_file`; the success voucher of W5 (`wd:{withdrawal_id}:PAID`, the snapshot channel's
cash subject, BR-WDR-09); `tax_ytd` (BR-WDR-20); wallet.withdrawal_changed, which sends the
member the result message; and an audit record (action withdrawal_resolve, with the
`withdrawal_id`, the status before and after, `resolution`, `channel_order_id` and `paid_at`; no
personal data and not the proof text). A member without a verified real name fails `tax_ytd`:
20001 with `data.fields=[withdrawal_id]` and `data.reason=resolve_identity_missing`, nothing
written, because the money was paid and this needs a person.

**`failed`** (BR-WDR-15): refunding money that actually left is a double payment, so every
condition is checked by the server and nothing in the request can vouch for one. In order,
the first that does not hold is 20001 with `data.fields=[resolution]` and its `data.reason`:

- `resolve_too_early`: less than 24 hours since T.
- `resolve_bill_unverifiable`: the bills of T's day and the next must both be downloaded and
  both lack this out_biz_no. There is no read yet that tells a downloaded bill without this
  line from a bill not downloaded, and not finding a line is never taken as absent.
- `resolve_query_unverifiable`: the latest query must be 「订单不存在」. That answer has no
  verified channel code yet and is recorded as unknown (BR-WDR-22, BR-WDR-28).

**So today every `failed` is refused, and nothing is written (D10-625, D10-626).** The target,
once the bill read and the code exist, is W10 to FAILED with `WITHDRAW:RETURN` and a
`withdraw_holds` row (`manual_failed_watch`, `withdraw.manual_failed_hold_days`, default 7) on
one transaction; that path comes with its own task and rule tests before the Alipay channel
opens. A wechat withdrawal has its own conditions (BR-WDR-33 ⑧) and is refused the same way
until then.

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with another
body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. 2xxxx refusals are not stored, so a fixed
request can reuse its key. The step-up token is a header and not part of the body hash, so a
replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

paid.summary: The proof shows the channel paid

value.proof_text: 查询返回订单不存在；当日与次日账单都没有

200.description: The withdrawal ended, or the first result of the same key.

post.summary: Reject one withdrawal and return its money to the balance (驳回)
post.description:
The 【驳回】 of the withdrawal review page and detail (01 F-ADM-07; BR-WDR-10, BR-WDR-09;
design/specs/admin-withdrawals.md; ruling D10-595). Permission point `withdraw.review`; a
super admin holds every point. Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request (AdminWithdrawalRejectRequest): `reason_code`, one of the five a person can choose
(RISK_SUSPECT, ORDER_ABNORMAL, PAYEE_INFO_INVALID, USER_REQUEST, OTHER); NEGATIVE_BALANCE
is written by the system only and fails at the schema. `note`, the internal note, at most
500 characters and not blank after trimming, required for USER_REQUEST (BR-WDR-10: a member
cancels through customer service, and the reason must be recorded). The member sees the text
of the reason code, never the note.

Order of checks: the route schema comes first, before the permission and step-up checks, as
on every admin route (D10-591): a body that fails it is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the
field, also for a caller without the permission point or a token, and nothing is written.
Then `withdraw.review` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → step-up (10003) →
a blank `note`, or none for USER_REQUEST, is 20001 with `data.fields=[note]` → an unknown
`withdrawal_id` or one of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[withdrawal_id]` (no 404) →
a withdrawal not in PENDING_REVIEW or APPROVED, or changed by another request, is 20902 with
`data.resource=withdrawal` (refresh) → a transfer attempt with result pending, success or
unknown is 20001 with `data.fields=[withdrawal_id]` and `data.reason=reject_attempt_exists`:
such a withdrawal ends only through BR-WDR-15 → while the switch
`payout.proven_success_writeoff.enabled` is on (default on), a withdrawal with
`hold_reason=payer_side_after_transfer` is checked against its latest query, because a
transfer the channel reported as failed may still have been paid (BR-WDR-08 W3, BR-WDR-17,
决-08 A): no query yet, or a latest query with an unknown result, is 20001 with
`data.fields=[withdrawal_id]` and `data.reason=reject_query_required`; a latest query that
succeeded is 20001 with `data.reason=reject_query_success`: the money went out, so this
withdrawal ends through W11 and rejecting it would pay twice. A latest query with result
fail, a status `payout.query_status_map` maps to a definite failure (BR-WDR-28), lets the
rejection through. BR-WDR-17 also allows 「订单不存在」, but that answer is recorded with result
unknown and has no verified channel code yet (BR-WDR-22, BR-WDR-28), so until one is
registered it is refused as reject_query_required like every other unknown result: the
safe direction. `payout.payer_side_codes` is also empty until verified, so no withdrawal
reaches this state before then. With the switch off this check does not run. Apart from
these, a transfer attempt that definitely failed does not stop a rejection.

Effects, in one transaction under the member's balance lock: W3 with `reject_reason_code`,
`reject_note`, `reviewer_id` the caller and `reviewed_at` the injected Clock; the voucher
WITHDRAW:RETURN moving the amount from frozen back to available (BR-WDR-09);
wallet.withdrawal_changed, from which the member gets the rejection message. Writes an audit
record (action withdrawal_reject, with the `withdrawal_id`, the status before and after, the
`reason_code` and the `note`; no personal data).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. A new key for a withdrawal
already rejected is 20902. The step-up token is a header and not part of the body hash, so
a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: The withdrawal rejected, or the first result of the same key.

get.summary: Monthly settlement bills of the app, page by page, newest bill month first
get.description:
The bill list of the settlement console (01 F-ADM-08 月结; 04 §3.2 settle_bills,
settle_batches; design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §1, §4). Read only, no step-up.
Permission point: any of `settle.bill` or `fund.view` (04 §11.1, §11.2); a super admin
holds every point. Each row is one settle_bills row of the console's app: `bill_id` (the
bill month M, YYYY-MM, BR-FUND-04 ③), the derived `status` (enum
admin_settle_bill_status; see AdminSettleBillStatus for the rule and for how the latest
round is read from settle_batches — derived at read time, not stored), `generation_started_at`,
`generated_at`, the bill-day totals `platform_order_counts`,
`platform_settle_commission_totals`, `beneficiary_total_fen`, `platform_retained_fen`,
`error_count` and `held_count`, the batch summary (`batch_count`, `draft_batch_count`)
and `created_at`.

The totals and the counts `error_count` / `held_count` of settle_bills reflect the
bill-day task only; supplement batches do not write them back (编排裁定 D10-280 ③,
BR-FUND-04 细则「补充批次」). They are for display only: every amount judgement and
reconciliation goes by the batch items (GET /admin/v1/settle-batches/{batch_id}/items),
never by these totals. The differences found by the consistency check (差错单) are not
listed by this resource; they are read through GET /admin/v1/recon-diffs.

Filters combine with AND: `bill_from` and `bill_to` (bill months YYYY-MM, both inclusive)
and `status` (the derived status at response time). A value outside the enum or the
pattern is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the parameter; `bill_from` later than
`bill_to` is 20001 with `data.fields=[bill_from, bill_to]`. A filter set nothing matches
is an empty page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error.

Order: `bill_id` descending. Pages with `page` (as AdminPage; a page past the last one is
`items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (above 200 is 20001, as AdminPageSize); `total` is the
count of the filter set. The Chinese names of the statuses come from the console
dictionary (BR-TEXT-25 admin_dict), not from this contract. Writes (confirm, schedule,
cancel a schedule, reject, continue execution, supplement batches, upload, check and
import of a union settlement statement) and the export are not part of this operation.
Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: One page of monthly settlement bills, newest bill month first.

get.summary: One monthly settlement bill with its bill-day totals and the summary of every batch
get.description:
The bill detail of the settlement console (01 F-ADM-08 月结; 04 §3.2 settle_bills,
settle_batches, settle_batch_items; design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §1, §4). Read
only, no step-up. Permission point: any of `settle.bill` or `fund.view` (04 §11.1,
§11.2). The fields of a list row (the derived `status`, the bill-day totals with
`error_count` and `held_count`, the batch summary), plus `batches`: every settle_batches
row of the bill, main and supplement, CANCELLED included, ordered by `created_at` then
`batch_id`. Each batch carries its columns (`batch_id`, `platform`, `kind`, `status`,
`settle_mode`, `scheduled_at`, `confirmed_by`, `confirmed_at`, `cancelled_reason`,
`order_count`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `paused_by_switch_at`, `created_at`,
`row_version`), `in_current_round` (whether it belongs to the bill's latest round as defined in
AdminSettleBillStatus, the batches the derived status is computed from) and `item_counts`, the count of its settle_batch_items
by item_type × result, summed at read time (not stored).

As on the list: the totals and the counts of settle_bills reflect the bill-day task only
and supplement batches do not write them back (编排裁定 D10-280 ③); they are for display
only, every amount judgement and reconciliation goes by the batch items. The
consistency-check differences are read through GET /admin/v1/recon-diffs, not here. A
bill whose platform had credit.enabled off at generation keeps only its check results
and has no batch for that platform; a bill with no batch at all is `issued` once
generated (AdminSettleBillStatus).

A `bill_id` that does not match ^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$, or for which the app has no
bill, is 20001 with `data.fields=[bill_id]` (no 404). Writes (confirm, schedule, cancel a
schedule, reject, continue execution, supplement batches, upload, check and import of a
union settlement statement) and the export are not part of this operation. Reading does
not write an audit record.

200.description: The bill with its bill-day totals, derived status and batches.

post.summary: Confirm every DRAFT batch of the bill, to run now or at a set time (SB2)
post.description:
The 【确认立即执行】 and 【定时执行】 of the bill detail (01 F-ADM-08 月结; BR-FUND-04 ⑥,
迁移表 SB2; design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §4). Permission point `settle.bill` (04
§11.2; `fund.view` alone is not enough). Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid
totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`. One person confirms.

One confirmation covers every DRAFT batch of the bill, whatever its round and platform,
never a choice of batches (BR-FUND-04 ⑥「一次确认该账单全部 DRAFT 批次」; 编排裁定
D10-444, which replaces the latest-round scope of D10-437 ② and D10-440). A batch can be
DRAFT outside the latest round: a schedule cancelled (SB3) after a later supplement launch
leaves it DRAFT with `in_current_round` false, and this confirmation covers it too. The
rounds of AdminSettleBillStatus only derive the bill's `status`, which can therefore differ
from what is waiting to be confirmed: go by the batches with `status` DRAFT, not by the
bill's `status`. Request:
`expected_batches`, one `{batch_id, expected_row_version}` per DRAFT batch of the bill,
taken from GET /admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id}, at most 1000 entries; `settle_mode`,
IMMEDIATE when absent, or SCHEDULED; `scheduled_at`, required with SCHEDULED and not
allowed with IMMEDIATE, later than the moment of confirmation and outside the nominal
asset snapshot window (BR-FUND-04 ⑥, BR-FUND-18).

Order of checks: `settle.bill` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001 with `data.fields` naming the field; `settle_mode` and
`scheduled_at` not fitting each other, or a time not allowed, is 20001 with
`data.fields=[scheduled_at]`) → a `bill_id` that does not match the pattern, an unknown
one or one of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[bill_id]` (no 404) → a bill still
generating is 20001 with `data.fields=[bill_id]` and `data.reason=bill_not_ready` → 20902
with `data.resource=settle_batch`, nothing changed (refresh the detail): `expected_batches`
is not exactly the bill's DRAFT batches (one missing, one extra, one twice, or the bill
has none), or an `expected_row_version` is out of date. `scheduled_at` is checked again
at the moment of confirmation, after the locks are taken; a time no longer allowed is the
same 20001 with `data.fields=[scheduled_at]`, nothing changed.

Effects, in one transaction: every DRAFT batch of the bill moves to CONFIRMED (SB2, a
compare-and-set on each `row_version`, `row_version` + 1), with `settle_mode`,
`scheduled_at` (null for IMMEDIATE), `confirmed_by` the caller and `confirmed_at` the
server's current time. Confirming only reaches CONFIRMED: execution is a later step (SB5,
BR-FUND-04 ⑦), and no money moves in this operation. Writes an audit record (action
settle_bill_confirm, with the bill, `settle_mode`, `scheduled_at` and each batch with its
status before and after; no personal data). The response is the bill as
GET /admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id} returns it afterwards.

No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): the compare-and-set makes a repeated submission a 20902.
The manual start (SB10, not open before the finance confirmation of BR-FUND-04), the
upload of a union settlement statement, a supplement pre-check and the export are not
part of this operation.

200.description: The bill after the confirmation.

post.summary: Launch a supplement check and its batches for one platform of a bill
post.description:
The 【发起补充批次】 of the bill detail (01 F-ADM-08 月结; BR-FUND-04 ⑧ ⑫;
design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §4). Permission point `settle.bill` (04 §11.2). Step-up:
totp tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`.

Request: `platform`, the one platform to check. The server checks that platform's orders
of the bill as the bill-day task does and generates DRAFT batches of kind supplement
(SB1). They form one new round (AdminSettleBillStatus, 编排裁定 D10-437) and are confirmed
through POST /admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id}/confirm, which covers every DRAFT batch of the
bill (编排裁定 D10-444).

Order of checks: `settle.bill` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001 with `data.fields=[platform]`) → a `bill_id` that does not
match the pattern, an unknown one or one of another app is 20001 with
`data.fields=[bill_id]` (no 404) → the launch guard, each refusal 20001 with `data.reason`,
nothing written: `credit_disabled` with `data.fields=[platform]` (the switch
`credit.enabled.<platform>` is off, BR-FUND-04 ⑨); `bill_not_ready` with
`data.fields=[bill_id]` (the bill is still generating, or the bill-day task has no result
for this platform on this bill); `pending_draft` with `data.fields=[bill_id]` (the bill
still has a DRAFT batch of any platform and any round, the requested one included;
先确认或驳回现有 DRAFT 再发起, and both work on it whatever its round, 编排裁定 D10-440,
D10-444). A CONFIRMED batch does not refuse the launch, SCHEDULED included; if its schedule
is cancelled after the launch it is DRAFT again and the same confirmation covers it.

`outcome`: `generated` = the check ran; `batch_ids` are the new batches. `batch_ids` may be
empty: nothing to include is not an error and no empty batch is generated (SB1).
`duplicate` = the launch had already been claimed for the same nominal moment (settle_jobs
unique key); nothing was generated and `batch_ids` is empty. Refresh the detail.

This operation has no compare-and-set, so `Idempotency-Key` is required, as on the
recon-diff close and write-off: same key and body → the first result, the same
`batch_ids`, without a second launch; same key with another body → 20901; same key while
still running → 40901. A deliberate second launch uses a new key. The step-up token is a
header and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

Effects: the check results, differences of the supplement run (registered as on the bill
day) and the batches with their items, in one transaction. The totals of settle_bills are
not written back (编排裁定 D10-280 ③). No money moves in this operation. Writes an audit
record (action settle_supplement_create, with the bill, `platform`, `outcome` and
`batch_ids`; no personal data). The supplement pre-check, the upload of a union settlement
statement and the export are not part of this operation.

200.description: The result of the launch, or the first result of the same key.

get.summary: The items of one settlement batch, page by page, in check order
get.description:
The batch items of the settlement console (01 F-ADM-08 月结; 04 §3.2
settle_batch_items; BR-FUND-04 ⑦ ⑫; design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §1, §4). Read
only, no step-up. Permission point: any of `settle.bill` or `fund.view` (04 §11.1,
§11.2). Each row is one settle_batch_items row of the batch: `id`, `item_type` (order =
a sub-order row, beneficiary = a beneficiary make-up item, BR-FUND-04 ⑫), `order_id`,
`user_id`, `role` and `beneficiary_credit_id` (beneficiary items only, null on order
rows), `settle_seq` (order_settlements.seq at check time), `b_settle_fen` (order rows;
null on a beneficiary item when not recorded), `amount_fen` (beneficiary items, the
amount recomputed at execution; null on order rows and before execution), `result`
(null while the item is not executed yet), `skip_reason` and `created_at`. A row carries
the user_id only, never a phone number. These rows are what every amount judgement and
reconciliation of a bill goes by (the settle_bills totals are display only, D10-280 ③).

Filters combine with AND: `item_type` and `result` (credited, skipped, deferred, or
pending = the item has no result yet, result null). A value outside the enums is 20001
with `data.fields` naming the parameter; a filter set nothing matches is an empty page.

Order: `settle_seq` ascending, then `id` ascending. Pages with `page` (as AdminPage) and
`page_size` ≤ 200 (as AdminPageSize); `total` is the count of the filter set. An unknown
`batch_id` or a batch of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[batch_id]` (no 404). The
upload, check and import of a union settlement statement and the export are not part of
this operation. Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: One page of the batch's items in check order.

post.summary: Cancel the schedule of a confirmed batch, back to DRAFT (SB3)
post.description:
The 【撤销定时】 of a batch (01 F-ADM-08 月结; BR-FUND-04 ⑥, 迁移表 SB3;
design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §4). Permission point `settle.bill` (04 §11.2; `fund.view` alone is not enough). Step-up: totp
tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request: `expected_row_version` is the batch's `row_version` from GET
/admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id}. Only a CONFIRMED batch with `settle_mode` SCHEDULED that has not started can
be cancelled.

Order of checks: `settle.bill` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001) → an unknown `batch_id` or a batch of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[batch_id]` (no 404) → 20902 with `data.resource=settle_batch`, nothing changed (refresh the detail):
`expected_row_version` out of date, or a batch that is not CONFIRMED, not SCHEDULED, or
already started.

Effects: the batch moves to DRAFT (SB3, `row_version` + 1): `confirmed_by`, `confirmed_at`
and `scheduled_at` are cleared and `settle_mode` returns to IMMEDIATE, so it must be confirmed
again before it can run. POST /admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id}/confirm covers it with every
other DRAFT batch of the bill, also when a later supplement launch has put it outside the
latest round (`in_current_round` false, 编排裁定 D10-444). `paused_by_switch_at` stays
(BR-FUND-04 SB3). Writes an audit record
(action settle_batch_cancel_schedule, with the batch and, before and after, its `status`,
`settle_mode` and `scheduled_at`; no personal data). The response is the batch's bill as
GET /admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id} returns it afterwards.

No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): the compare-and-set makes a repeated submission a 20902.

200.description: The bill of the batch after the change.

post.summary: Reject a DRAFT batch with a reason (SB4)
post.description:
The 【驳回】 of a batch (01 F-ADM-08 月结; BR-FUND-04 ⑥, 迁移表 SB4;
design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §4). Permission point `settle.bill` (04 §11.2; `fund.view` alone is not enough). Step-up: totp
tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request: `expected_row_version` is the batch's `row_version` from GET
/admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id}. `reason`, required: after trimming surrounding whitespace 1–200 characters,
else 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`. Only a DRAFT batch can be rejected.

Order of checks: `settle.bill` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001) → an unknown `batch_id` or a batch of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[batch_id]` (no 404) → 20902 with `data.resource=settle_batch`, nothing changed (refresh the detail):
`expected_row_version` out of date, or a batch that is not DRAFT.

Effects: the batch moves to CANCELLED, a terminal state (SB4, `row_version` + 1), and
`cancelled_reason` records the trimmed reason. The orders of the batch stay WAITING and its
items and the ledger are not touched. Writes an audit record (action settle_batch_reject,
with the batch, the reason and, before and after, its `status`; no personal data). The
response is the batch's bill as GET /admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id} returns it afterwards.

No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6): the compare-and-set makes a repeated submission a 20902.

post.summary: Continue a PARTIAL batch after the switches are back on (SB8)

The 【继续执行】 of a batch (01 F-ADM-08 月结; BR-FUND-04 ⑦, 迁移表 SB8;
design/specs/admin-settle-bills.md §4). Permission point `settle.bill` (04 §11.2; `fund.view` alone is not enough). Step-up: totp
tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request: `expected_row_version` is the batch's `row_version` from GET
/admin/v1/settle-bills/{bill_id}. Only a PARTIAL batch can continue.

Order of checks: `settle.bill` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → body (20001) → an unknown `batch_id` or a batch of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[batch_id]` (no 404) → 20902 with `data.resource=settle_batch`, nothing changed (refresh the detail):
`expected_row_version` out of date, or a batch that is not PARTIAL → the guard, each refusal

get.summary: Daily asset snapshots of the app, page by page, latest snapshot day first
get.description:
The asset snapshot list of the fund console (01 F-ADM-08 资产快照; 04 §3.2
asset_snapshots, asset_snapshot_receivables; BR-FUND-18; design/specs/admin-fund-dashboard.md
§1, §4 — the daily ledger is the snapshot view, its fields follow this resource). Read
only, no step-up. Permission point: `fund.view` (04 §11.1, §11.2 资金看板); a super admin
holds every point. Each row is one asset_snapshots row of the console's app — the
snapshot of accounting day D written at D+1 00:01:00 +08:00 (BR-FUND-18): `snapshot_date`
(D), `total_available_positive_fen`, `total_negative_fen`, `total_frozen_fen`,
`total_waiting_fen`, `total_estimated_fen`, `waiting_comparable`, `receivables` (the
asset_snapshot_receivables rows of the snapshot: `platform` and `union_receivable_fen`,
ordered by platform code) and `created_at` / `updated_at`. The amounts are integer fen
exactly as the snapshot wrote them; they are not recomputed from the current balances or
orders. The balance totals cover the ledger entries with accounting_date ≤ D; the waiting
and estimated totals are the order states at the time the snapshot ran (BR-FUND-18).

A day whose snapshot has not been written (before D+1 00:01, or still pending) simply
has no row: it is not filled with zeros and is not an error. Reading never triggers or
rewrites a snapshot.

Filters combine with AND: `date_from` and `date_to` (snapshot days YYYY-MM-DD, both
inclusive). A value not matching the format is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the
parameter; `date_from` later than `date_to` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[date_from, date_to]`. A filter set nothing matches is an empty page
(`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error.

Order: `snapshot_date` descending. Pages with `page` (as AdminPage; a page past the last
one is `items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (above 200 is 20001, as AdminPageSize); `total`
is the count of the filter set. Not part of this operation: the daily ledger with W, P
and the water-level state (BR-WDR-18, depends on the union collection entry), the union
collection entry itself (`fund.cash_entry`), the fund dashboard and reports, and the
export. Reading does not write an audit record.

200.description: One page of daily asset snapshots, latest snapshot day first.

get.summary: Union collection records, page by page, latest collection day first
get.description:
The 联盟回款记录 table of the fund ledger page (01 F-ADM-08; BR-FUND-20 细则「联盟回款凭证」;
design/specs/admin-fund-dashboard.md §2). Read only, no step-up. Permission point:
`fund.view` (04 §11.1); a super admin holds every point. Each row is one collection
record of the console's app (04 §3.2 union_receipts): `receipt_date`, `platform`,
`amount_fen` (BR-FUND-20), `method` (ADMIN_ENTRY 后台录入 or R1_RECON R1 对账确认),
`cash_account`, `voucher_id` (凭证号, the link to the balance history) and who entered it,
`created_by` and `created_by_name`, both null for a record confirmed by R1 without an
operator. A reversed record stays in the list with its amount: `reversed_at`, `reversed_by`
and `reversal_voucher_id` are all set once it is reversed and all null until then.

Filters combine with AND: `platform`, `date_from` and `date_to` (collection days
YYYY-MM-DD, both inclusive). A platform outside the enum or a value not matching the
format is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the parameter; the route schema answers that
before the permission check, as on every admin route (D10-591). After the permission
check, `date_from` later than `date_to` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[date_from, date_to]`. A filter set nothing matches is an empty
page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error.

Order: `receipt_date` descending, then `created_at` descending, then `receipt_id`
descending. Pages with `page` (as AdminPage; a page past the last one is `items=[]`) and
`page_size` ≤ 200 (above 200 is 20001, as AdminPageSize); `total` is the count of the
filter set. Reading does not write an audit record.

post.summary: Enter one union collection and post its voucher (录入联盟回款)
post.description:
The 【录入联盟回款】 dialog of the fund ledger page (01 F-ADM-08; 04 §11.2 `fund.cash_entry`;
BR-FUND-20 and its 细则「联盟回款凭证」; design/specs/admin-fund-dashboard.md §2, §6). Permission
point `fund.cash_entry`; a super admin holds every point. Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34):
without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`. The entry of
the enterprise Alipay balance W, under the same permission point, is not part of this
operation: it belongs to the payout console (BR-WDR-18).

Request (AdminUnionReceiptCreateRequest): `platform`; `receipt_date`, the day the money
arrived (YYYY-MM-DD); `amount_fen`, integer fen > 0, the amount of BR-FUND-20;
`cash_account`, the subject debited, CASH_ALIPAY or CASH_BANK (BR-FUND-20 细则); `note`,
optional, at most 500 characters and not blank after trimming; an outside serial number
goes here. Who entered the record comes from the session; `method` is always ADMIN_ENTRY
here, the request does not carry it.

Order of checks: the route schema comes first, before the permission and step-up checks,
as on every admin route (D10-591): a body that fails it is 20001 with `data.fields` naming
the field, also for a caller without the permission point or a token, and nothing is
written. Then `fund.cash_entry` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → the checks on a body that fits the schema (20001 with `data.fields`
naming the field: a blank `note`; a `receipt_date` later than the current accounting day of
the injected Clock, +08:00, with `data.fields=[receipt_date]`; CASH_BANK while 银行卡通道未开通,
with `data.fields=[cash_account]`). An earlier `receipt_date` has no lower bound. The amount is
not compared with the receivable (BR-FUND-20): a difference shows up in R1, this operation
opens none.

Effects, in one transaction: settlement (funds) writes the record to 04 §3.2 union_receipts
(`method=ADMIN_ENTRY`) with its UNION_RECEIPT voucher (BR-FUND-20 细则「联盟回款凭证」) through
the ledger command; the console calls the funds port. No user balance moves and W does not
change (BR-WDR-18). Writes an audit record (action union_receipt_create, with the
`receipt_id`, the platform, `receipt_date`, `amount_fen`, `cash_account` and `voucher_id`;
no personal data).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a header
and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key. There is no
business key: two records with the same platform, day and amount under different keys
are two collections. One collection is entered once (BR-FUND-20 细则) by reading the
platform's records of the last 30 days first (design/specs/admin-fund-dashboard.md §6); R1
shows a difference, and a record entered by mistake is reversed with POST
/admin/v1/union-receipts/{receipt_id}/reverse and entered again.

200.description: The collection record with its voucher, or the first result of the same key.

post.summary: Reverse one union collection record as a whole (红冲)
post.description:
The 【红冲】 action of a row of the 联盟回款记录 table (01 F-ADM-08; BR-FUND-16, BR-FUND-20 细则
「联盟回款凭证」; design/specs/admin-fund-dashboard.md §4, §6). 代理补全的默认，待财务确认
(D10-538), as the voucher of the entry itself. Permission point `fund.cash_entry`; a super
admin holds every point. Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Only the whole record is reversed and a record is reversed once; there is no partial
reversal and no amount in the request. To change an amount, reverse the record and enter
it again with POST /admin/v1/union-receipts. A record of either `method` can be reversed.
Request (AdminUnionReceiptReverseRequest): `reason`, required.

Order of checks: the route schema comes first, before the permission and step-up checks,
as on every admin route (D10-591): a body that fails it is 20001 with `data.fields` naming
the field, also for a caller without the permission point or a token, and nothing is
written. Then `fund.cash_entry` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → a `reason` blank after trimming (20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`) → an
unknown `receipt_id` or one
of another app is 20001 with `data.fields=[receipt_id]` → a record already reversed is
20902 with `data.resource=union_receipt` (a record can be reversed once, BR-FUND-16; the
console refreshes and shows 已红冲; the unique constraint on the reversal voucher answers
the same under a race). The reversal is not compared with the balance of the cash subject
or of the receivable.

Effects, in one transaction: settlement (funds) posts the reversal voucher (uniq_key per
BR-FUND-16, BR-FUND-20 细则) through the ledger command and sets `reversed_at`, `reversed_by`
and `reversal_voucher_id` on the record (04 §3.2 union_receipts); the original record and
voucher stay. No user balance moves and W does not change (BR-WDR-18). Writes an audit
record (action union_receipt_reverse, with the `receipt_id`, the platform, `amount_fen`,
`voucher_id`, `reversal_voucher_id` and `reason`; the table has no reason column, the audit
record holds it; no personal data).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. A new key for a record already
reversed is 20902. The step-up token is a header and not part of the body hash, so a
replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: The reversed record, or the first result of the same key.

post.summary: Enter the available balance W of a payout channel (录入企业支付宝余额)
post.description:
The 【录入企业支付宝余额】 dialog of the payout console and the fund ledger page, and the same
dialog for the WeChat operating account (01 F-ADM-07, F-ADM-08; BR-WDR-18 and its 细则「W 的
取数时刻」「多通道的 W」; 04 §3.2 payout_watermarks; design/specs/admin-payouts.md §2;
rulings D10-223, D10-241, D10-248, D10-285, D10-592). Permission point `fund.cash_entry`; a
super admin holds every point. Step-up: totp tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request (AdminPayoutWatermarkCreateRequest): `channel`, alipay or wechat; bank_card opens
with its channel and fails at the schema until then (D10-592, as D10-538 ⑥). `available_fen`,
integer fen ≥ 0, the balance read off the account. `measured_at`, the moment it was read
(t_W). `note`, optional, at most 500 characters and not blank after trimming. Who entered it
comes from the session.

Order of checks: the route schema comes first, before the permission and step-up checks,
as on every admin route (D10-591): a body that fails it is 20001 with `data.fields` naming
the field, also for a caller without the permission point or a token, and nothing is
written. Then `fund.cash_entry` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) →
step-up (10003) → the checks on a body that fits the schema, each 20001: a blank `note`
with `data.fields=[note]`; and with `data.fields=[measured_at]`, compared with the injected
Clock, a `measured_at` more than 5 minutes after now (BR-WDR-18 细则, D10-241, D10-248), more
than 2 hours before now, or before the channel's latest `measured_at` (design/specs/
admin-payouts.md, 代理补全的默认, D10-592). Up to 5 minutes ahead counts as clock skew and is
accepted; the same `measured_at` as the latest is accepted. These are checked here and not
by a database constraint (D10-241). Entries of one channel are checked one at a time, so
two racing requests cannot both pass on the same latest row.

Effects: one new row of 04 §3.2 payout_watermarks, written by payout and never changed;
`entered_by` is the admin_users id of the caller. The latest row by `measured_at` is the W
that the next execution of that channel judges (BR-WDR-18 ①②③), and it goes stale 2 hours
after `measured_at`. No voucher, no balance, no withdrawal changes. Writes an audit record
(action payout_watermark_create, with the `watermark_id`, `channel`, `available_fen`,
`measured_at` and `note`; the table has no note column, the audit record holds it; no
personal data).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result; same key with
another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. The step-up token is a header
and not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: The row entered, or the first result of the same key.

post.summary: Group the chosen withdrawals into a batch and execute it (批量自动打款、执行所选)
post.description:
The 【批量自动打款】 of the withdrawal review page and the 【执行所选】 of the payout console (01
F-ADM-07; BR-WDR-11, BR-WDR-12, BR-WDR-18; design/specs/admin-withdrawals.md,
admin-payouts.md; ruling D10-595). Permission point `payout.execute`; a super admin holds
every point; the executor may be the reviewer of the same withdrawal (ADD-05). Step-up: totp
tier (BR-ID-34): without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.

Request (AdminPayoutBatchCreateRequest): `withdrawal_ids`, 1 to 200 ids without duplicates
(200 is 代理补全的默认, D10-595; a duplicate is 20001 with `data.fields=[withdrawal_ids]`).

Order of checks: the route schema comes first, before the permission and step-up checks, as
on every admin route (D10-591): a body that fails it is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the
field, also for a caller without the permission point or a token, and nothing is written.
Then `payout.execute` (10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`) → step-up (10003) →
the duplicate check. After that the answer is 200, and whether the batch ran is in the data.

One transaction, the three steps of BR-WDR-12:

- ① The whole batch is refused when `payout.enabled` is off or `payout.queue_paused` is on.
- ② Each id is judged under its row lock: still APPROVED; no withdrawal block of the member
  (BR-WDR-05); no transfer attempt of any result; its channel enabled and not paused. An id
  that does not pass stays APPROVED, or whatever status it had, and is listed in `left`. An
  unknown id, one of another app or one that is not a UUID is listed with `not_approved`,
  the same as one that left APPROVED; a non-UUID id never reaches the database.
- ③ The watermark of what passed, per channel (BR-WDR-18, D10-285, D10-288). When what
  passed is all on one channel, a failure refuses the whole batch: `rejected`, no
  withdrawal moves, nothing is sent. When it spans several channels, a failing channel's
  withdrawals stay APPROVED and are listed in `left` with the watermark reason, while the
  other channels run; if every channel fails, the outcome is still `executed`, with `paying`
  empty.

Answer (AdminPayoutBatchResult): `outcome` is `executed` or `rejected`. `executed`:
`batch_id`, the new batch (kind=manual); `paying`, the ids that moved APPROVED → PAYING (W4),
possibly none; `left`, the others with `reason` (not_approved, member_blocked,
has_transfer_attempt, channel_disabled, or a watermark reason on a batch of several
channels). `rejected`: `reason` (payout_disabled, queue_paused, watermark_stale,
watermark_below_forecast, watermark_usable_exceeded), `channel` for a watermark reason, and
`batch_id` null, `paying` and `left` empty.

Effects of `executed`: an APPROVED withdrawal already on another batch is moved to the new
one first by a CAS and the old batch keeps its item as moved_out (BR-WDR-12), including one
listed in `left` with member_blocked, has_transfer_attempt or channel_disabled; one left
with not_approved or a watermark reason is not moved. A withdrawal left with any reason but
not_approved that was on no batch joins the new one (`batch_id`, BR-WDR-11, D10-609), so a
later batch moves it and this one records moved_out. A `rejected` answer writes none of this,
and not_approved never joins. Each paying withdrawal gets
`executor_id` the caller, `executed_at` the injected Clock and `execute_seq` + 1, its
transfer job on the same transaction and wallet.withdrawal_changed. No voucher here: the
money stays frozen until the result (BR-WDR-09). The transfer itself runs in the payout
process, which reviews each withdrawal again and may hold it (W9, BR-WDR-13). Writes an
audit record for either outcome (action payout_batch_execute, with the `outcome`, the
`batch_id` or `reason`, and the counts and ids of `paying` and `left`; no personal data).

`Idempotency-Key` is required: same key and body → the first result, a `rejected` one too;
same key with another body → 20901; same key while still running → 40901. After fixing what
refused a batch (a fresh W, say), submit with a new key. The step-up token is a header and
not part of the body hash, so a replay after a 10003 keeps its key.

200.description: Whether the batch ran, or the first result of the same key.

executed.summary: One withdrawal moved to PAYING, one left

rejected.summary: The whole batch refused by the watermark

get.summary: Payout switches, limits and each channel's water level, computed when read
get.description:
The status cards of the payout console (01 F-ADM-07; BR-WDR-11, BR-WDR-17, BR-WDR-18;
design/specs/admin-payouts.md §2; ruling D10-595). Read only, no step-up. Permission point:
any of `payout.execute` or `fund.view`; a super admin holds every point. Reading does not
write an audit record. Every figure is limited to the app of the console and read fresh, with
the same configuration defaults EXECUTE uses.

`payout_enabled` and `queue_paused` are the switches of BR-WDR-12 ①. `single_cap_fen`,
`daily_cap_fen` and `daily_sent_fen` are the limits of BR-WDR-18 and today's (+08:00) sum of
kind=transfer attempts with result pending, success or unknown, across channels, as the
pre-transfer review counts it (BR-WDR-13 ③). `watermark_usable_bp` is
`payout.watermark_usable_bp`.

`channels` has alipay, bank_card and wechat, in that order: `enabled` and `paused` are
`payout.channel_enabled.<channel>` and `payout.channel_paused.<channel>`; `watermark`,
`forecast_withdrawal_fen` and `water_level` mean what they mean in GET
/admin/v1/fund-ledger, per channel (D10-285): `watermark` is null until a row exists, never a
default; no recent withdrawals give a forecast of 0, not null; `water_level` is `low` when W
is below 1.5 P, else `normal`, and null when there is no W or it has passed the 2 hour limit,
while `watermark.measured_at` still shows its age.

Not part of this operation: the queue and the unknown results (their lists), and changing a
switch (adminUpdateKillSwitch).

200.description: The overview at this moment.

get.summary: Fund ledger overview, computed when read
get.description:
The overview cards of the fund ledger page (01 F-ADM-08; BR-FUND-20, BR-WDR-18;
design/specs/admin-fund-dashboard.md §1, §2). Read only, no step-up. Permission point:
`fund.view` (04 §11.1); a super admin holds every point. Reading does not write an audit
record. Every figure is limited to the app of the console.

Computed when read, from all the entries posted so far, not from the last asset snapshot:
`as_of` is the moment of the reading. `receivables` is the 已入账未回款 per platform, the
balance of UNION_RECEIVABLE:{platform} (BR-FUND-20), ordered by platform code, only
platforms with at least one entry, and it can be below 0 after a collection above the
receivable; `union_receivable_total_fen` is their sum. `negative_total_fen` is the sum of
the magnitudes of the negative available balances (the negative_fen side of BR-FUND-18) and
`negative_user_count` the number of accounts behind it. With no entries yet these
are `receivables=[]` and zeros.

The water level fields are null when there is no data, never filled with a default.
`watermark` is the latest W of the enterprise Alipay channel; W is entered on the payout
console (BR-WDR-18) and is the owner's material, so it is null until a row exists.
`forecast_withdrawal_fen` is P of BR-WDR-18 for the same channel, null while the payout side
does not provide it; no recent withdrawals give 0, not null. `water_level` is the
conclusion from W and P: `low` when W is below the alert line of BR-WDR-18, else `normal`.
It is null when W or P is null or when W has passed the staleness limit of BR-WDR-18,
as a conclusion from an old W would mislead; `watermark.measured_at` still shows its age.

Not part of this operation: the daily ledger (the asset snapshots, GET
/admin/v1/asset-snapshots), the records (GET /admin/v1/union-receipts), the alert lines
and other cards of the water level, and the fund dashboard adminGetFundsReport.

200.description: The fund ledger overview at the moment of reading.

noWatermark.summary: W not entered yet, so W, P and the conclusion are null

withWatermark.summary: W, P and the conclusion available

get.summary: Registered emergency switches and their current values
get.description:
Permission point: any of `switch.all`, `switch.payout` or `switch.pay` (04 §11.2; read
only, no step-up). One row per switch the server has registered (04 §10.2, one row per
concrete key such as `convert.enabled.taobao`), in registry order, page by page (`page`,
`page_size` ≤ 200): the current value (null = never written, the registered `default`
applies), the value type and, for `enum`, the allowed values, the permission points of
which any one may change it (`permissions`), whether the console may change it at all
(`admin_editable`; false for `agent.whitelist_only` and `agent.model_route`; true for
`withdraw.auto_payout.enabled` means it can only be turned off, `true` is refused), and the
`version` that PUT /admin/v1/kill-switches/{key} takes as `expected_version`. Rows the
account may not change are still listed, so the console can show them read only.

put.description:
Permission point by key (04 §11.2), any one of the listed points suffices:
`withdraw.enabled`, `payout.enabled`, `payout.queue_paused`,
`payout.channel_enabled.<channel>` and `payout.channel_paused.<channel>` need
`switch.all` or `switch.payout`; `pay.enabled` and `pay.channel_enabled.<pay_channel>`
need `switch.all` or `switch.pay`; every other switch, `withdraw.auto_payout.enabled`
included, needs `switch.all`. Lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. `withdraw.auto_payout.enabled` can only be turned
off from the console (BR-WDR-30: off is the safe direction): `false` follows the rules
here, `true` is 20001 with `data.fields=[value]`; turning it on needs the owner's
confirmation, a separate flow outside this operation. Step-up: totp tier for every key, clearing
`payout.queue_paused` and `payout.channel_paused.<channel>` included (04 §11.2, BR-ID-34):
without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.
A key the server has not registered, or one the console may not change
(`agent.whitelist_only`, `agent.model_route`; `admin_editable=false`), is 20001 with
`data.fields=[key]`; a value of the wrong type or outside `options` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[value]`. CAS: `expected_version` is the switch's `version` the console
showed (0 for a switch never written); every change adds 1 and a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=kill_switch`, refresh and retry (04 §6.6). Writing the value the switch
already has with a matching version succeeds without change, version bump, audit or
alert. `reason` is optional (at most 200 characters) and kept in the audit record.
Every change is written to the audit log (action kill_switch_change, before and after
values) and pushes an alert; it takes effect on every server instance within 10 seconds
(04 §10.2). No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

get.summary: Registered configuration items and their current values
get.description:
Permission point: any of `config.general`, `config.risk` or `config.business` (04 §11.2;
read only, no step-up). One row per configuration key the server has registered (04 §10),
in registry order, page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200): the current value (null =
never written, the server's built-in default applies), the value type and, for `enum`,
the allowed values, the permission point that guards changing it (`permission`), whether
the console may change it (`admin_editable`; false for `agent.page_guide.routes` and
`external_hosts` until their editors ship) and the `version` that the writes take as
`expected_version`. Emergency switches (04 §10.2) are not here but under
/admin/v1/kill-switches.

post.summary: Change several configuration items at once
post.description:
Permission point: the one point that guards every key of the batch (`config.general`,
`config.risk` or `config.business`, 04 §11.2); a batch mixing keys of different points
is 20001 with `data.fields=[items]`, as is a key listed twice. Step-up by that point
(04 §11.2, BR-ID-34): none for `config.general`; totp tier for `config.risk` and
`config.business` (without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`). The whole batch takes effect or nothing does (05 F1-10): first every
key and value is checked (unregistered or not admin-editable keys, values of the wrong
type, outside `options` or failing the key's own rule such as the candidate set of
BR-AI-01 细则「页面引导」), and any failure is 20001 with `data.fields` listing every
failing key; only then are the versions compared, and any mismatch is 20902 with
`data.resource=config_item` and nothing applied. Each changed key gets its version plus
1, a history version and an audit record (action config_item_change) carrying the
shared `reason`; the change pushes an alert. Values take effect as each key's reader
re-reads it (within that key's cache period), never retroactively (04 §10). No
Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

get.description:
Permission point: any of `config.general`, `config.risk` or `config.business` (04 §11.2;
read only, no step-up). Every stored version of the item, newest first, page by page
(`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200), with the value, who wrote it (null = written by the system)
and the reason given; any older version can be restored with POST
/admin/v1/config-items/{key}/rollback. A key the server has not registered is 20001 with
`data.fields=[key]`.
